chapters.title: Chapter 1169. I Own the Underlayer, the Corridor, and the Last Year of Your Life
paragraphs: Apollo collapsed inward, pressing both palms against his face as if he could physically squeeze the revelations out of his brain. His breathing was shallow, ragged gasps that sounded like tearing parchment.
The world was tilting; the ground beneath him felt like it was dissolving into static.
"And the emergency council," Rex continued, his voice cutting through Apollo’s self-imposed silence like a scalpel.
He showed no mercy, no pause for Apollo to catch his breath. "The session where Morwenna stood up, her face flushed with righteous fury, and accused me directly of being Tremor."
"She was correct... She was the only one in that entire room with enough spine and enough intellect to assemble the pieces properly."
Rex let out a soft, almost fond hum. "And what happened, Apollo?"
"Do you remember? I sat there, calm as a saint, while Elizabeth, Aurelia, and you rose to my defense."
"You argued for my innocence with such conviction it was almost touching..."

"By the time the gavel fell, Valentina had formally cleared me of all suspicion... That was the single most enjoyable hour of my life." Rex’s voice dropped to a conspiratorial whisper. "Four separate people whom I had personally ruined, whom I had personally slaughtered, stood up one after another to explain why I couldn’t possibly be responsible."
"The one person telling the truth was shouted down by the very people I had broken."
"Stop." Apollo’s voice was a broken wheeze.
"Then you said Celestina’s name out loud," Rex said, ignoring the plea. "The entire network buckled... Panic set in... And then I stepped in."
"I gave a speech, a beautiful, rousing speech that stitched the network back together. And afterward?"
"Everyone thanked me... They thanked me for saving the meeting."
"For being their rock in the storm." Rex’s mouth curved into a grotesque parody of a smile. "I have been thanked, Apollo... formally... and even publicly."
"I have received commendations for cleaning up every single mess I created."
"I said stop!" Apollo screamed, the sound tearing from his lungs, raw and bleeding.
He looked up, his face a mask of agony and hatred, blood dripping from a split lip onto his chest. "Make it stop, Rex! Please!"
"You asked for the scale, Apollo," Rex said, his violet eyes flaring with sudden, terrifying intensity. "I am giving you the scale..."
"Do not beg for mercy when you asked for understanding."
Rex’s tone shifted then.
The cruelty remained, but it was layered with something almost... tender. A perverse sense of pride.
"And then there was Theo."
Rex paused, tilting his head as if reminiscing about a cherished childhood memory. "That one... that was my masterpiece..."
"I took him apart over the course of a month... But not with blades, not with fire..."
"No, that would have been too simple... I took his life apart piece by piece."
"I dismantled his standing in his household, his position as heir, his grandmother’s affection, his aunt’s trust, his mother’s attention, and Diana’s."
A shudder passed through Rex’s frame. "I removed them one by one, making each loss seem like nothing more than a cruel twist of natural consequence rather than a calculated campaign.
"By the end of that month, he was standing at the edge of the eastern cliff with absolutely nothing left—no family, no future, no self..."
"And he stepped off. He chose the fall."
Rex’s eyes darkened, the violet light bleeding into the black. "Kaeleth caught him on the way down."
"The god saw a broken boy and handed him a designation because a desperate deity needed a disposable weapon."
"And what did I do, Apollo...? I beat that weapon."
"I broke what Kaeleth made."
Rex took a step closer, the magical pressure in the domain becoming so heavy that Apollo felt his bones creak under the weight of the air itself. "Then I went into Kaeleth’s domain."
"I fought him, I broke him, and I reached into his chest with my own bare hands and tore his temporal authority over Aethelgard right out of his soul."
"I’ve been holding it quietly ever since... Nobody on the surface has any idea."
Rex leaned down, his breath cold against Apollo’s ear. "The entire city, every heartbeat, every sunrise, every passing second... the whole city runs on borrowed time."
"And that time belongs to me."
The silence that followed was not empty; it was heavy, a physical weight that pressed down on Apollo like the depths of an ocean. It was a suffocating, pressurized quiet that rang in his ears.

Apollo looked like a man drowning in an endless sea of poisoned information. His pupils were blown wide, unfocused, and darting erratically as his brain tried and failed to reconcile the Rex he loved with the monster standing before him.
His breathing had become a series of wet, irregular spasms. His ribs screamed with every shallow inhalation, the bone fragments grinding together like broken glass in his chest.
Rex let him suffer in that silence for several agonizing seconds. He wanted Apollo to feel the full weight of the void before he filled it with more horror.
Then, with terrifying grace, Rex stepped closer. He crouched down until their eyes were level, forcing Apollo to meet that violet, inhuman gaze.
This proximity was intimate, almost tender, which made the words all the more devastating.
"The Underlayer," Apollo said suddenly.
His head jerked up, a spark of desperate, dying fire flickering in his eyes. "You said you were allied with them."
"Out there, in the corridor... you told me you came from below..."
"Was that—"
"I don’t just ally with them, Apollo," Rex interrupted, his voice smooth as silk and cold as ice. "I own it... they’re all my bitch."
He said it with the casual detachment of a man mentioning a piece of property he held in a portfolio. "And of course... completely."
"Mordecai kneels to me like a lowly pest... Every survivor of the purge... the purge that systematically erased anyone who refused to bend kneels to me.
"Down there, in the dark, they whisper the name Lord Xerollion..."
"The man you’ve been fighting for the last half hour, the one you think is some rogue warlord?"
"He is merely my instrument... He is the supreme authority of two hundred thousand souls who have never once seen my actual face."

Rex leaned in closer, the violet glow from his eyes casting dancing, demonic shadows across Apollo’s pale skin. "The army standing out there in that corridor right now, the one your soldiers are bleeding to hold back?"
"That is mine. I ordered them into position."
"I designed the very geometry of the corridor you’re standing in."
"Every angle, every choke point, every tactical advantage—it was all calculated by me."
"The Key." Apollo’s voice had gone utterly flat, the sound of a man who had already died inside. "Elizabeth’s Key..."
"The artifact that saved us from the breach."
"Built to my specifications," Rex said with a delighted chuckle. "Using materials I personally sourced and supplied."
"It opened at an anchor point I calibrated myself, while Elizabeth watched me work, thanking me for my ’strategic insight.’"
"Your entire army marched through a door I built, into a corridor I chose, to fight a force I command."
Rex’s smile widened, revealing teeth that seemed too white, too perfect. "You have been inside my plan since the morning you stood on that platform and gave your speech."
"Every decision you made today, every order you shouted, every soldier you positioned to defend this ground—it wasn’t courage, Apollo... It was obedience."
"You were simply taking the steps I laid down for you in advance."
Apollo made a small, broken sound, a whimper that died before it could become a word. His hands clutched at the violet ground, his fingernails cracking against the pulsing surface.
He felt small. He felt like an insect caught in a web, realizing too late that the spider hadn’t been hunting it; it had been playing with its food.

Rex crouched directly in front of him again, elbows resting on his knees in a posture of casual relaxation, as if they were two old friends sharing drinks in a tavern rather than a god killer and a broken hero in a realm of madness.
"And now," Rex said, his voice dropping to a quiet, almost compassionate murmur, "we come to the part I know is going to hurt you the most."
"The part that will finally break what’s left of your mind."
He paused, letting the tension coil like a spring between them.
"Veylor... Calivara... Eryndra..." Rex spoke their names like sacred relics. "All three of them died by my hand... directly."
"No proxies. No elaborate accidents. No poisoned wine or staged ambushes."
"I stood before them... I looked them in the eye... And I killed them personally."
"And I want you to understand something, Apollo..." Rex’s expression became terrifyingly blank. "I did not hesitate... Not once..."
"With any of them."

chapters.title: Chapter 1170. My Heir Is Growing Inside the Woman You Called Mother
paragraphs: Apollo made a strangled noise, a sound that shouldn’t have come from human vocal cords. It was something caught between a wet sob and a feral, animalistic growl.

His fist slammed down against the violet floor of the domain with such desperate force that the consecrated surface spider webbed beneath his knuckles, sending cracks racing outward like lightning through glass.
Blood seeped from between his fingers where the impact had split his skin.
"But the others," Rex continued, his voice carrying that infuriatingly thin, razor-edged grin.
He was enjoying this slow, methodical dissection of a hero’s psyche. "Talyra. Aisella. Mireya. Nerith..."
"Those four aren’t dead as you can see..."
"Death would have been a waste of resources, Apollo... They were always far more useful alive."
"What do you mean..." Apollo whispered.
The words barely existed; they were ghosts of sounds. His mind was already racing ahead, anticipating the shape of the monster’s next strike, but his heart refused to believe it.
He was already braced for the impact.
"I took them from you," Rex said.
There wasn’t a single gram of remorse in his tone; there wasn’t even a flicker of guilt. It was the statement of a collector describing how he acquired rare specimens. "One at a time."
"I orchestrated it with the precision of a clockmaker... do I have to repeat myself?"
Rex leaned forward, savoring the moment. "Talyra and Aisella on the island."
"Remember that undead attack? The one you all mourned as a tragic stroke of misfortune?"
"That was the moment when I ’heroically’ chose to save them instead of securing the artifact."
"I arranged that entire assault... I deployed those constructs myself from the Underlayer two days before the first corpse even fell."
"I created the crisis so I could play the savior and claim your precious women as my spoils."
Apollo’s breathing became a series of ragged, choking gasps. Each word felt like a physical blade twisting in his gut.
"Mireya," Rex said, tilting his head as if recalling a pleasant dinner. "I acquired her through leverage."
"She witnessed me executing Legion prisoners who had already surrendered, men who had laid down their arms."
"She saw what I truly was, and I made sure she understood that her continued safety depended entirely on her cooperation."
"By the time the leverage was no longer necessary, she didn’t want to leave..."
"She had become complicit. She had become mine."
Rex’s eyes gleamed with a sadistic light. "And Nerith..."
"At the edge of that gorge in the canyon... While you were all convinced I was helping your expedition, guiding you through the treacherous terrain...
"I was simply positioning her... I was making sure she was exactly where I needed her to be."
Apollo’s eyes went empty. The light behind them didn’t just dim; it extinguished.
Apollo’s gaze was hollow, reflecting the emptiness of a man who had looked into the sun and discovered it to be made of ice.
Every revelation was a theft. Every word Rex spoke was reaching inside Apollo’s chest and tearing out a piece of his past.
Rex could see it happening in real time; the man was reviewing months of memories like a film strip being fed through a shredder.

Rex recalled the quiet mornings when he felt safe, the celebration dinners that made him feel loved, Talyra’s hand resting on his arm during long meetings, and the sound of Nerith’s laughter echoing across a campfire.
Every fond recollection, every warm moment of connection, was being contaminated. They weren’t memories anymore; they were evidence.
They were data points in Rex’s grand design.
"They love me," Rex said, closing the final inch between their faces.
His breath was hot against Apollo’s cheek, a mockery of intimacy. "That wasn’t an act, Apollo..."
"That wasn’t manipulation either... They actually love me... They... chose me."
Rex’s voice dropped to a venomous murmur. "And they have continued to stand by your side this entire time, pretending to be loyal friends and trusted allies, but only because I asked them to."
"Because it was useful to me to have them close to you... I needed them to watch your every move."
"I needed them to study your every hesitation, your every fear, and report every single weakness you possessed straight back to me."

The revelation was the final blow. It wasn’t just that his friends were spies; it was that his deepest vulnerabilities had been harvested by the people he trusted most, all under the direction of the monster who had orchestrated his entire life.
The last thread of Apollo’s sanity snapped with the sound of a breaking bone.
Apollo broke.
It was not the contained, stifled weeping from earlier. That had been the sound of a man trying to hold himself together.
This was something else entirely, something primal and devastating. The sound that tore from Apollo’s throat was a raw, unfiltered howl of pure, unadulterated anguish.

It wasn’t just one voice; it sounded like a chorus of the damned, echoing off the impossible absence of walls in the domain, folding back over itself until it sounded like dozens of people were grieving in perfect, horrific unison.

Apollo doubled forward, his spine arching in pain, his forehead slamming against the pulsing violet floor. His fingernails clawed uselessly at the consecrated surface, seeking purchase in a reality that would not tear and escape from a truth that would not leave.
He screamed until his vocal cords shredded, until his voice cracked into a wet, bleeding rasp, and yet he kept screaming a sound of a soul being flayed alive from the inside out.
Rex stayed crouched in front of him. He didn’t flinch and he didn’t look away.

His eyes glowed with a faint, predatory violet light, watching every spasm, every convulsion of grief with an expression of deep, quiet, unhurried satisfaction. This was a connoisseur watching a masterpiece unfold.
He had planted this seed months, perhaps years ago. He had watered it with patience, with calculated cruelty, with the steady drip of false kindness.
The time had come for the harvest, and Rex intended to savor every single grain.
He waited. He waited until the howling had eroded into ragged, hitching sobs that sounded like breaking glass.
Only when Apollo was physically spent, trembling and broken on the floor, did Rex speak again. His tone was as level and unremarkable as a man commenting on the weather.
"There’s one more I haven’t mentioned," Rex said.

His head tilted a fraction, as though he were genuinely weighing whether to continue, playing with the last shred of Apollo’s dignity. Then, the grin spread across his face wide, cruel, and hungry. "Amelia."
Apollo’s entire body locked. The shivering stopped instantly, and the air in the domain seemed to freeze.
His head came up slowly. The hollow emptiness in his eyes was gone, replaced by something far worse: a new fear.

It was smaller, sharper, and infinitely more personal. It was the particular terror of a man who had just realized there was one final door in his house, and he had forgotten to check if the monster was already inside.
"My mother," Apollo whispered.
His voice was paper-thin, cracking with a terror that made his hands shake uncontrollably. "Don’t, Rex, please... don’t tell me—"
Rex let out a soft, mocking laugh. "Oh, Apollo... You always were so slow and so... blissfully naive."
Rex leaned in closer, his voice dripping with venomous amusement. "You spent your life thinking you were the noble protector, the righteous son."
"But even your ’righteousness’ couldn’t save her from the truth."

"How does it feel, I wonder? Knowing that while you were out playing hero, chasing glory and pretending to be the world’s savior, your precious High Priestess was learning exactly how to kneel to a real power?"
Rex’s eyes flashed with sadistic delight. "You always did have excellent taste, though..."
"I suppose I should thank you for passing down those instincts... It made her so much easier to break."
"Stop it," Apollo breathed, tears streaming down his face, mixing with the blood from his split lip. "Stop it, you bastard!"

"Why? Because it’s true?" Rex cut in, his voice sharpening like a blade. "Months ago, High Priestess Amelia Brightsoul, the most respected figure in the Temple of Life, the beacon of purity you worshipped, had belonged to me since long before any of this."
"She didn’t need to be coerced, Apollo... She needed to be awakened."
Rex’s grin became something demonic, stretching too wide for a human face. "And she’s not alone in her devotion."
"She’s carrying my child right now..."
"My heir is growing inside the woman you called ’Mother.’"

chapters.title: Chapter 1171. Watching a Good Man’s Morality Burn Away Was the Whole Point
paragraphs: The silence that followed Rex’s revelation was not merely an absence of sound; it was a physical entity. It was a vacuum that seemed to suck the very oxygen out of the domain, leaving Apollo gasping in a space that had suddenly become impossibly small and infinitely hostile.
Apollo stared up at Rex. Whatever was happening on his face could no longer be described as grief.
Grief was human; grief was something that could be mourned. What was surfacing now was something older, darker, and far more dangerous.
The tears still tracked through the blood and grime on his cheeks, but underneath them, something ancient was rising through the wreckage of his psyche.
The trembling that had been born of heartbreak moments ago had transformed. It was no longer the shuddering of a broken man; it was the violent, tectonic vibration of something about to detonate.
"You," Apollo said.
His voice had dropped to a register so low it felt like a vibration in the bones rather than a sound. It was rough, serrated, and shaking with a lethal intensity.
"You... touched... my mother."
"I did considerably more than touch her, Apollo," Rex answered.
There was no regret, no hesitation, only the obscene enjoyment of watching the last vestiges of Apollo’s humanity burn away. "Touch is for strangers..."
"But for lovers... there is something much more... thorough."
"And I assure you, she was happier about it than any of the others."
"She found a comfort in me that your ’righteousness’ could never provide."
"Say it isn’t true," Apollo whispered. He wasn’t shouting.
That was somehow worse than the quiet desperation of a man clinging to a single thread of reality before it snapped. "Look at me... Look me in the eye and tell me you’re lying about her!"
"You’ve admitted to every atrocity, every betrayal, every murder today!"
"Lie about this one thing... Just this one thing, Rex...!"
"Lie to me, and I swear to whatever gods are left that I will believe you...!"
Rex didn’t blink. His violet eyes remained fixed on Apollo with predatory calm.
"She’s about four months along, Apollo..."
"She’s been keeping it quiet, playing the part of the grieving, exhausted High Priestess."
"The Temple thinks she’s been unwell, that the divine light is taxing her body... They have no idea they’re worshipping a womb for my legacy."
Something behind Apollo’s eyes finished dying. The last spark of the boy who believed in heroes, the last fragment of the man who believed in loyalty, vanished into a black abyss.
The golden light around Apollo didn’t just brighten; it fractured.
It was not the controlled, harmonious aura he had carried throughout their entire confrontation. This was raw, unmediated output.

It was energy screaming out of his body without direction, without shape, flaring in jagged, violent pulses that threw harsh, demonic shadows across a floor that had never known darkness before. The sound was a sickening, continuous, low-frequency hum that made the teeth ache and the ears bleed.
CRACK.
Fresh fissures split outward from beneath Apollo’s knees, spider webbing through the pulsing violet surface in a radial web three meters wide.
The domain itself gave a low, guttural groan of protest, a sound of structural agony as its young, unanchored reality registered a magical pressure it had never been designed to contain.
The air around Apollo began to distort, shimmering with heat haze as his power began to cook the very atmosphere.
"You took everyone I love," Apollo said.

His voice began to climb, gaining terrifying force with every syllable. Each word carried the weight of a collapsing star, echoing through the emptiness with a devastating power that made the domain tremble.
"You killed my friends like they were nothing more than insects..."
"You destroyed Theo’s entire life, breaking his mind until he had no choice but to throw himself off that cliff..."

The gold light intensified, turning from amber to a blinding, searing white that began to char the edges of the violet floor. Blood began to weep from Apollo’s nose and ears as his own power began to tear his body apart from the inside.
"You put your hands on my mother," he roared, the sound cracking like thunder. "And you did all of it while smiling at me..."
"While pretending to care... While letting me call you brother..."
Rex did not flinch. He did not retreat in fear. Instead, he stood up with a slow, deliberate grace and stepped back several paces, maintaining a measured distance.
He moved without any sense of urgency, his movements fluid and unhurried, as if he were merely adjusting his position to get a better view of a gallery painting.
His violet eyes remained fixed on Apollo, watching the transformation with the focused, clinical fascination of a scientist observing a volatile chemical reaction finally reaching its critical point.
This was the culmination. This was the entire purpose.
The grief had been delicious—a fine wine to savor—but grief was passive. Grief was the aftermath.

What Rex craved was this: the exact, exquisite moment where a good man’s morality burns away like dross in a furnace, leaving behind whatever primal, terrifying thing had been buried beneath the surface all along.
As Apollo’s power swelled, Rex felt something strange. The domain began to pulse with a foreign distress.
It wasn’t a conscious feeling, but a distant, systemic shudder that vibrated through his own magical essence. It was as if a limb he owned was suddenly experiencing phantom pain.
The system’s warnings began to flicker at the periphery of his consciousness, unbidden and insistent.
[Warning: Domain stability degrading.]
[Anchoring principle undefined.]
[Structural integrity at seventy-one percent and falling.]
Rex glanced at the notification and dismissed it with a flick of his mental attention. He felt no fear.
If the domain collapsed, it collapsed. They would simply be thrown back into the reality of the corridor, surrounded by ten thousand witnesses to their confrontation.
It would be inconvenient, yes, a messy complication in his perfect design, but survivable. He refused to interrupt this moment to go and repair his own architecture.
He would not break the spell now. Not for anything.
"I am... not going to forgive you," Apollo said. His voice was no longer a scream; it was something worse.
It was quiet, absolute, and carried the finality of a death sentence.
Apollo began to rise. The movement was agonizing to watch.
His body was a ruined vessel beneath the divine light, muscles torn, bones cracked from the sheer pressure of his own ascending power, and ribs grinding against one another.
But he forced himself up, each inch of movement a battle against gravity and pain. When he finally stood fully upright, the air around him seemed to solidify.

The golden light had stabilized, but it was no longer a soft glow. It had compressed into a hard, tight sheath of searing energy that burned millimeters from his skin, crackling with the sound of superheated metal.

"Not now... Not later... Not ever," Apollo continued, his eyes locked onto Rex’s with a hatred so pure it felt like it could melt stone. "You can kill me here, in this void, where no one will ever hear my bones break..."
"You can erase me from existence, and you might succeed..."
"But I refuse to die quietly knowing that something like you is still walking around in a world I was sworn to protect."
Then, the energy began to corrupt.
It started as a tremor in the light. The pure, sanctified gold began to bleed.

Something dark, viscous, and arterial red started to thread through the golden veins. It moved like living blood through arteries, pulsing in a slow, sickly rhythm that was completely out of sync with the divine cadence of his power.
Where the gold touched the floor, the cracks attempted to seal, the instinct of life affinity seeking to repair the damage. But where the red touched the floor, the domain screamed.
CRUNCH.

The red energy didn’t heal the fractures; it fed them. The cracks spiderwebbed outward with violent force, widening from three meters to six, then ten, tearing through the violet consecrated surface like teeth through flesh.

The pattern was no longer random damage. The fractures began to arrange themselves into something deliberate, something geometric and grotesque, spreading outward from Apollo’s feet like something ancient and hungry was growing out of the very foundation of reality.

chapters.title: Chapter 1172. He Self-Authored a Power the System Couldn’t Even Name
paragraphs: Rex’s eyebrow rose fractionally. For the first time since this performance began, the mask of detached amusement slipped, revealing something sharper: genuine curiosity.
That was new. Life affinity was a constant; it was predictable, nourishing, and harmonious.
It obeyed the laws of growth and preservation. Whatever Apollo was manifesting now defied every fundamental law of the magic Rex understood.

It wasn’t the goddess’s gift, nor was it the structured power of his own designation. When Rex activated his Divine Perception, scanning the anomaly with genuine, focused attention, the system stuttered.
The reading didn’t return a clean category; it returned a corrupted error. This was not magic granted by a higher power; this was something manufactured from the raw, bleeding marrow of a human soul.
It was a power born directly from the deepest, most necrotic point of the suffering Rex had spent the last twenty minutes meticulously constructing.
"You said I was too good to deserve this," Apollo said.
His voice had gone past anger, past grief, and even past hatred. It had gone cold—a temperature so absolute it felt like the heat was being sucked out of the room.
"You said my goodness was a weakness..."
"That it kept me from seeing what I truly was..."
Apollo’s head tilted back, and for a moment, he looked like something other than human. His jaw unhinged in a silent scream before the sound finally broke free.
"AAAAAAAAGGHHHHHHHHHH!!!"
The scream was inhuman. It wasn’t a vocalization; it was a seismic event.
It started as a guttural roar from his diaphragm and escalated into a piercing, glass-shattering shriek that seemed to tear through the fabric of the domain itself.

Apollo’s muscles corded and bulged to the point of tearing through his skin; blood began to seep from his pores as his circulatory system struggled to contain the sheer pressure of the energy surging through him.

His eyes rolled back, showing only whites stained crimson by ruptured capillaries. He screamed for what felt like an eternity, a sound of endless, unceasing torment that demanded vengeance from the very stars.

"All right, then," Apollo growled between ragged, wet gasps, his voice echoing with a dual tonal distortion, his own voice layered beneath something deeper and more ancient. "Let’s find out how much of that ’goodness’ I can burn away to make you pay."
"For every friend... For every tear... For her..."
The eruption came a second later.

It wasn’t a flash; it was a detonation. The gold and red light exploded outward from Apollo’s center in one enormous, violent exhale that shook the entire domain to whatever passed for its foundations.
The unanchored structure groaned audibly, a sound like grinding tectonic plates as the violet pulse of the floor stuttered and skipped like a dying heartbeat.
BOOM.

The shockwave hit Rex like a physical wall of heat and pressure, but he didn’t move. The brightness was absolute, a supernova contained within a confined space that swallowed every detail of the world for a full second and a half.
The air screamed as it was displaced and superheated into plasma, and the sound of the explosion lingered as a high-pitched ringing that threatened to burst eardrums.
When the light finally began to recede, peeling back like burning paper to reveal what lay beneath, Rex was still standing exactly where he had been.

His feet were planted, his hands were loose at his sides, and that infuriating, hungry grin remained etched across his face. His violet eyes glowed brighter than ever, fixed with absolute, undisguised anticipation on the crater of shattered reality where Apollo had stood.
Rex didn’t care about the structural damage. He wasn’t concerned about the fading stability of his domain.

He only cared about what would emerge from that scorched circle. Because whatever was about to walk out of that light was something new, something terrifying, something broken, and something he had created.
And it had been a very long time since anything had truly surprised him.

The light did not dissipate; it sank. Instead of fading into the atmosphere, the searing gold and arterial red imploded inward, flowing back into Apollo like water down a drain, condensing until it settled beneath his skin.
Apollo stood in the center of the cratered, fractured floor, and the man who had stood there moments ago was gone.

The change was not a monstrous transformation; there were no wings, no scales, and no grotesque mutations, but the shift was terrifyingly visible. His physique had hardened; the muscle across his shoulders and arms was corded and dense, standing out like carved granite beneath his skin.
His flesh carried a faint, sickly luminescence, as though the energy coursing through his veins had become so pressurized it was beginning to burn through his epidermis.

His eyes remained gold, but the irises were no longer pure; at the center of each pupil burned a core of molten, deep crimson. When he blinked, the red lingered like the dying glow of embers behind closed eyelids.
The divine white sheath of the goddess remained, but it had been utterly subjugated. It no longer sat atop him like a garment; it had been woven into the new, darker tapestry of his power.
It ran through the veins of his new magic, folded into a working that had been forged from raw hatred and fed by a source far less sanctified than any celestial pantheon.
Rex activated Divine Perception, pushing his targeted analysis function to its absolute breaking point. The system stuttered, processing data that seemed to violate the very logic of the universe.
[Working type: UNCLASSIFIED.]
[Source: SELF AUTHORED.]
[Divine component present but subordinate.]
[Emotional substrate: PRIMARY POWER SOURCE.]
[No existing designation match found.]
[No pantheon signature detected.]
Rex read the text twice. His pupils dilated.
’Self authored.’

Apollo Brightsoul, the paragon of obedience, the man who had spent his entire life operating within the predefined parameters of a goddess’s blessing, had just committed an act of metaphysical heresy.
He had created something from nothing, using nothing but the scorched remains of his own soul and the agony Rex had so carefully cultivated.

Whatever the divine framework thought about mortals producing original, divine class workings out of pure, unadulterated grief, the system was too late to intervene. The blasphemy was already complete.
Rex found himself smiling. It wasn’t the cruel smirk of a manipulator anymore; it was the genuine, unguarded smile of a man who had finally found something worth playing with.
"This isn’t about saving Aethelgard anymore," Apollo said.
The voice was wrong. It was a dual-tonal nightmare, his own voice layered beneath a subsonic growl that seemed to vibrate from the floor itself.
"This isn’t about justice... This isn’t about duty..."
He took a step forward, and the fractured ground beneath his boot shattered further.
"This is about making sure you feel even a fraction of what you’ve given me."
He moved.
It wasn’t a run. It wasn’t a leap.
It was a sudden, violent displacement of space.
One moment Apollo was twenty meters away; the next, he was a blur of gold and crimson streaks cutting through the air.
Rex was ready. His mind screamed warnings before Apollo even shifted.
Foresight had mapped the trajectory two full seconds in advance. Adaptation was already recalibrating his magical defenses to counter the unknown energy signature.
His Peak Superhuman Physique had already begun the micro adjustments in his stance to pivot and evade. His brain was already executing the perfect counter maneuver.
But Apollo was moving faster than Rex’s ability to process the causality of the attack.
WHAM.
The punch didn’t just connect; it detonated against Rex’s jaw. The sound was like two slabs of marble colliding at supersonic speeds—a wet, bone-crushing CRACK that echoed through the domain.

The sheer force of the impact bypassed Rex’s magical barriers as if they weren’t there, transferring directly into his skull. His head was snapped sideways with such violence that his neck vertebrae audibly groaned under the strain.

Rex’s entire body followed a quarter second later, launched backward like he had been struck by a siege engine. He tore through three separate formations of Rex’s drifting light, each one shattering like glass upon impact.
He skidded across the fractured violet floor, his shoulder grinding against the jagged edges of the domain’s surface, sparks flying where flesh met magical stone.
He slid another eight meters, leaving a trail of blood and displaced energy behind him, before finally coming to a bone-jarring halt.
Blood trickled from the corner of Rex’s mouth, staining his chin as he gasped for air, his enhanced senses struggling to reassemble the reality that had just been violently torn apart.

chapters.title: Chapter 1173. Whatever You Built to Get Around Defenses Doesn’t Work Here
paragraphs: Rex lay motionless for several heartbeats, his body sprawled across the fractured violet floor. His mind was not focused on the pain; pain was merely data but on the rapid-fire assessment of his own deteriorating condition.
’Jaw fractured in two places.’
’Left clavicle hairline crack.’
’Rib three bruised.’
’Shoulder joint compromised.’
He could feel his Infinite Regeneration working, a familiar hum of cellular reconstruction beginning to stitch his tissues back together. But something was wrong.
The process felt sluggish and even heavy. The usual instantaneous knitting of bone and sinew was being met with something viscous and resistant.
That red energy that self-authored blasphemy wasn’t just attacking him physically; it was interfering with the very mechanism of his immortality.
It was poisoning the acceleration of his healing, forcing his body to work through a metaphorical mire of crimson sludge.
’Interesting,’ Rex thought, a cold thrill running through his spine. ’That is very, very interesting.’

With a grunt of effort that sounded more like amusement than agony, Rex forced himself upright. His movements were precise despite the damage, the mechanical efficiency of a predator refusing to acknowledge injury.
He raised his thumb to his mouth, wiping away the smear of crimson that stained his lips, and stared at the blood coating his skin.
"Better," Rex said, his voice smooth despite the grinding of his broken jaw.
He deliberately placed the blood-stained thumb in his mouth, sucking the copper-tasting liquid off it while maintaining unflinching eye contact with Apollo.
The gesture was calculated with sadistic precision, a provocation designed to remind Apollo that even in defeat, Rex remained the master of this game.
"I’ve been waiting for you to show me this since the moment we started..."
"I was wondering when you’d stop pretending to be a saint and start being a weapon."
Apollo did not answer. He didn’t even blink.
The man who had once offered forgiveness now offered only annihilation.
He came again.
The approach was a violation of physics that made Rex’s enhanced senses recoil. Apollo didn’t run in any conventional sense; he didn’t push off the ground with muscles and sinew.
Instead, the red gold energy surrounding him seemed to contract the space between them. The distance between twenty meters and Rex’s face didn’t disappear; it collapsed.
One moment Apollo was a distant silhouette of burning rage; the next, he was a screaming comet of divine fury.
Rex reacted instantly. His body twisted, his reflexes honed by centuries of combat theory, but the speed of the attack was beyond his predictive models.
Apollo’s shoulder slammed into Rex’s left side with the force of a falling star.
CRUNCH.
A wet, sickening pop echoed through the domain as Rex’s shoulder dislocated, the bone tearing through the surrounding ligaments.

Rex didn’t scream. In mid-motion, as his body spun from the impact, he reached up with a clawed hand, grabbed his own arm, and violently wrenched the joint back into its socket with a brutal, self-inflicted snap.
But Apollo was already mid swing, a follow-up strike fueled by momentum and hatred. Rex raised his forearm to block, but the impact was catastrophic.
His radius and ulna shattered audibly under the pressure, the bones splintering into fragments that pierced through his own muscle.
’Pain is irrelevant,’ Rex’s inner monologue hissed. ’Counterattack now.’
Using the momentum of his own collapsing defense, Rex drove his knee upward with every ounce of his supernatural strength. The strike connected squarely with Apollo’s ribcage.
THUD CRACK.
The impact was devastating. Rex felt the satisfying give of ribs snapping like dry kindling, followed by the wet squelch of internal organs rupturing under the concentrated pressure.
For a split second, Apollo’s breathing faltered, a momentary lapse where his lungs failed him. But even as Rex prepared to follow up, Apollo’s body reacted with horrifying efficiency.

Somewhere between the second and third seconds of the impact, the ruptured organs began to knit back together, reforming even as Apollo’s fist was already whistling through the air toward Rex’s temple.
Rex ducked, the wind of the punch ruffling his hair, and slid backward across the cracked floor to create distance. His breathing was ragged now, his body a map of fresh trauma.

"That’s twice now," Rex panted, sliding until he regained his footing, buying himself half a second of breathing room. "Whatever you built in that furnace of yours, it’s prioritizing recovery over raw output."
"Your body is fixing itself faster than it can break..."
"That’s either some deep-seated survival instinct, or it’s a very calculated decision..."
"I’d genuinely like to know which one it is."
Apollo stood his ground, his stance wide and unshakable. The red at the center of his eyes wasn’t just glowing; now it was pulsing, bleeding light into the air around him like smoke from a pyre.
"It’s neither," Apollo said, his voice a terrifying harmony of man and monster. "It’s not instinct, and it’s not a choice."
He took another step, the floor beneath him disintegrating into fine violet dust.
"I’m simply not going to stop. Whatever my body has to do to keep me moving is my problem."
"Your problem is what happens when I finally reach you."

The sequence of violence that followed was not a duel; it was an execution attempt. The disciplined, textbook precision that had defined Apollo for twenty-five minutes—the elegant Academy techniques, the measured stances, and the controlled magical flows—was dead.
In its place was something primal, something feral. What emerged from the red gold haze was a combatant who had abandoned all pretense of form.

His punches were thrown from impossible, bone-breaking angles that no instructor would have approved, each strike delivered with a raw, unrefined savagery that had stopped respecting the difference between a martial strike and an act of demolition.
Every blow Apollo landed carried a dual catastrophe.
First came the heat, a searing, white-hot agony that didn’t just burn the skin but bored through flesh like molten lead, chewing through muscle fibers and melting marrow.
But beneath that thermal destruction lay something far more insidious: the old, familiar reverse entropy of Apollo’s original Life affinity.
It ran beneath the burn like a parasitic current, pulling tissue backward into an earlier state of cellular existence while the heat simultaneously destroyed it forward.
It was a temporal paradox made manifest in violence, a wound that was being healed and incinerated at the exact same moment.

Rex’s mind raced, his consciousness struggling to process the anomaly. Full Potential Adaptation whirred at maximum capacity, its neural pathways firing like lightning as it attempted to map this new threat.

In a single night against a god, Rex had mastered seventeen distinct temporal mechanisms, but this was different. His system would acquire the pattern for the thermal burn, only to immediately lose the thread because the life affinity component kept shifting the context beneath it.
He was trying to catch smoke with his bare hands.
For the first time in his second life, Rex lost control of the tempo.

For two brutal minutes, Rex fought back with everything he had. He didn’t unleash his full output, for doing so would be suicidal, but he pushed himself to the level he had utilized against Kaeleth, unleashing a torrent of coordinated magical assault.
SHRAKK BOOM!
Rex’s Telekinesis seized the loose formations of domain light, compressing them into superheated projectiles.

He launched them with the force of railgun slugs. They struck Apollo’s center mass with wet, concussive impacts that should have shattered his ribcage, but the projectiles simply dissipated against the crimson aura, rocking Apollo half a step before he steadied.
Rex pivoted, his eyes glowing with lethal intent.
’Gravity: Forty Gs.’
’Focused Cone.’
"Down," Rex hissed.
The localized gravitational well slammed into Apollo like an invisible hammer, driving him to one knee with enough force to crack the domain’s foundation.
For exactly one and a half seconds, Apollo was pinned, his knees grinding into the violet stone. But then, the red gold energy began to writhe.

Like liquid fire climbing a mountain, the energy surged up the gravitational gradient, defying the crushing weight, and forced Apollo back to his feet. He stood unbowed, his breathing steady despite the impossible pressure.

Desperate, Rex pivoted to a more fundamental attack. He tapped into an original elemental frequency, the same destructive vibration that had annihilated three stacked barrier workings earlier that night.
He channeled it into a concentrated beam of pure molecular disruption.
VROOOOOM ZAP!
The beam washed over Apollo’s torso, searing a path of charred flesh across his chest. But before Rex could even finish the mental incantation to follow up, the wound closed.
The flesh knitted together, the charred edges reforming into smooth skin in a heartbeat.

Apollo took a step forward, the air around him distorting from the sheer intensity of his presence. When he spoke, the dual registers of his voice created a dissonant chord that vibrated in Rex’s very teeth.
"That doesn’t work anymore," Apollo said.
There was something profoundly wrong about hearing such a simple observation delivered with that inhuman cadence. "Whatever you built to get around defenses, it was built to get around defenses."
"This is different, Rex."
Apollo’s eyes burned brighter, the crimson cores expanding until they seemed to swallow his irises.
"This isn’t a defense," Apollo growled, his fist clenching as sparks of red gold energy arced between his fingers. "There’s nothing here for you to get around..."
"There’s only what I can break."

Rex stood his ground, blood dripping from his shattered forearm, his breath coming in measured gasps. He felt the irritation of being outmaneuvered, but beneath that, beneath the adrenaline and the pain, there was something else: a deep, intoxicating fascination.
Apollo wasn’t just fighting him; he was rewriting the rules of engagement in real time.

chapters.title: Chapter 1174. I Laughed Because Defeat Was the Only Language He Understood
paragraphs: The terrifying realization settled into Rex’s mind with the cold clarity of a blade: the working Apollo had produced was not a barrier, nor was it a shield or an absorption mechanism. Those were external layer tools that could be dismantled, bypassed, or severed.
This was different. This was a fundamental change in state. Apollo had not merely equipped a new power; he had converted his entire metaphysical existence into something else entirely.
There was no longer a seam between the man and the effect where an intervention could be inserted.
Rex’s Energy Manipulation function screamed in warning. Twenty minutes ago, it had found a promising fracture between Apollo’s innate affinity and the goddess’s divine layer.

Now, that function went hunting for the same vulnerability, only to recoil. That crimson current pulsing through Apollo’s veins had welded the two components together into a single, seamless, continuous structure.
To attack the magic now was to attack the flesh, and to attack the flesh was to attack the magic. They were one and the same.
’Fine,’ Rex thought, his jaw grinding as his teeth knitted back together. ’If I can’t unravel the weave, I’ll just try to tear the loom apart.’
Rex abandoned his complex magical constructs. He went back to fists, because fists were honest.
Fists did not rely on layers of theory; they relied on mass, velocity, and the brutal reality of impact.
For ninety seconds, the center of the collapsing domain became a slaughterhouse of kinetic energy. It was the most vicious, unmitigated stretch of physical exchange either of them had ever endured.
Rex was objectively faster; Rex was objectively better. That was a fundamental truth that remained unshaken.
His technique remained flawless even as Apollo’s degenerated into raw, desperate swinging.
Rex’s reads remained two full seconds ahead, allowing him to dance through the storm of Apollo’s fury, landing three precise, devastating strikes for every one he was forced to absorb.
But physics had become an enemy.
It did not matter that Rex landed more strikes. It did not matter that his technique was superior.
Because Apollo’s singular, unrefined blow carried more destructive potential than Rex’s three calculated counterattacks combined. The math of the fight had been corrupted.
WHACK CRUNCH.

Rex drove a knife hand into the side of Apollo’s neck with enough force to collapse the carotid artery. He watched, clinical and detached, as the crimson light flooded the wound, reknitting the vessel before the blood pressure could even begin to drop.
The artery sealed as quickly as it had torn.
SNAP.

Rex pivoted, catching Apollo’s left arm in a vicious joint lock. With a sharp twist of his hips, he executed a perfect break, the elbow joint exploding outward in a spray of cartilage and bone fragments.

But Rex couldn’t savor the victory. Four seconds later, he had to release the arm when the bone began to reset itself while still trapped within his grip, the regenerating limb snapping back into place with such violent force that it nearly shattered Rex’s own wrist.
THUD.
Rex drove his heel sideways into Apollo’s knee, feeling the patella shatter and the ligaments tear apart. But as the joint collapsed, Apollo’s free fist found Rex’s sternum.
BOOM.
The impact was like being struck by a runaway train. Rex felt his ribs buckle and crack inward, the pain white-hot and all-consuming.

He was launched thirty meters across the fractured domain, tumbling through the air before crashing into a pillar of light. All the while, he could see Apollo already standing, the ruined knee rebuilding itself beneath his trousers even as the man stepped forward to pursue.
Rex rolled onto his side, coughing up thick ropes of blood. His own ribs were already beginning to click and pop as they finished their rapid reset, the pain fading into a dull, manageable ache.
He looked up at Apollo through the haze of blood and sweat, his expression almost conversational.
"You’re healing faster than I am," Rex observed.
His voice was steady, almost academic, despite the carnage. "That’s twice today... The rate of cellular regeneration is outstripping my own compensatory adaptation."
"I’m going to be thinking about that for a while."
Apollo didn’t pause. He didn’t slow down.
He moved through the debris like an inevitable force of nature, his eyes two pits of burning, molten hatred.
"I hope it’s the last thing you think about," Apollo growled, the dual tones of his voice promising nothing but the end.
The next assault was not a strike; it was a cataclysm. Apollo descended like a falling god, his fist wreathed in that unstable, crimson gold corona.
When his hammer strike connected with Rex’s shoulder, the sound wasn’t just a crack; it was a thunderclap that shook the very foundations of reality.
BOOM CRASH!

The force drove Rex downward with such obscene velocity that he didn’t just hit the floor; he obliterated it. He punched through layers of crystallized domain light and reinforced violet stone, plummeting into the dark void beneath the platform.
The floor beneath them failed to reconstitute. That section of the domain simply stayed broken, a jagged, bleeding wound in a reality that was already unraveling.
The anchoring principles of the space were buckling under the sustained, divine adjacent pressure of their conflict, leaving behind a ragged crater that screamed of instability.
Rex didn’t even have time to register the fall before Apollo was above him.
WHAM!
A knee connected with Rex’s face before he could even right himself. The impact was wet and sickening.
Rex’s head snapped back, vertebrae grinding against each other with a sound like gravel in a blender. Blood sprayed from his nose and mouth in a crimson mist as he was propelled upward from the hole.
But the onslaught was relentless. As Rex scrambled to find purchase, Apollo’s fist found his ribcage.
CRACK SQUELCH.

Four ribs shattered simultaneously, the bone fragments driven inward like shrapnel. The accompanying heat was so intense it cauterized the wound instantly, turning the surrounding muscle tissue into blackened, charred meat.
Rex’s internal systems went into emergency override: ’Regeneration protocols engaged. ’

But there was a delay, a terrifying three-second lag, where his body had to prioritize clearing the necrotic, burned tissue before it could even begin the delicate work of knitting the bone back together.
In those three seconds, Rex was vulnerable. And it felt raw like a human.
Apollo exploited it with merciless efficiency.

Another knee buried itself into Rex’s abdomen. The force was so concentrated it lifted Rex off the ground entirely, sending him hurtling through a secondary light formation that shattered like glass upon contact with his body.
Rex spun through the air, a tangle of broken limbs and bloodied flesh, before slamming into a debris pile.
Before he could even draw breath, Apollo was there. An elbow caught Rex across the temple.
SHLICK.

The impact split Rex’s scalp clean open, peeling the skin back to reveal the pale white of the skull beneath. Blood flooded his vision, crimson rivulets pouring into his eyes, leaving him trapped in a nauseating world of double vision.
In a fight moving at Mach speeds, two seconds of blindness wasn’t just a disadvantage; it was a death sentence.
And yet, through the haze of pain, through the taste of copper and the scream of his own nerves, Rex laughed.
It was a wet, gurgling sound, but it was unmistakable.
That was the trigger. That was what truly broke Apollo’s composure.

It wasn’t the defiance, the strategy, or the tactical genius; it was the laughter. Every time Apollo slammed him into the earth like a broken doll, Rex came crawling back up with a blood-slicked grin that mocked the very concept of defeat.

Every time a strike landed with enough force to liquefy a normal man’s organs, Rex made a small, almost appreciative noise, a hum of approval, as though Apollo had simply played a particularly difficult chord on a piano.
"Come on," Rex wheezed.

His voice was a ruined rasp; Apollo had landed a blow square across his throat moments earlier, crushing the larynx before the regeneration could rebuild the cartilage. "That’s it...? Harder than that!"
Rex spat a glob of blood onto the shattered floor and leaned forward, his eyes bright with a terrifying, manic hunger. "I know you’ve got more hatred stored in there, Apollo."
"I can feel it pulsing... I put most of it there myself when I broke you."
The mockery in his tone was razor sharp, cutting through the divine fury like a poisoned blade.
Apollo’s reaction was primal. His face contorted, the red light in his eyes bleeding outward until his entire head seemed to be composed of nothing but burning rage.
He didn’t speak and he didn’t roar. He simply became motion.
He hit Rex again. And then he did not stop.

It was a wet, gurgling sound, but it was unmistakable.
That was the trigger.
That was what truly broke Apollo’s composure.
It wasn’t the defiance, the strategy, or the tactical genius; it was the laughter.
Every time Apollo slammed him into the earth like a broken doll, Rex came crawling back up with a blood-slicked grin that mocked the very concept of defeat.

Every time a strike landed with enough force to liquefy a normal man’s organs, Rex made a small, almost appreciative noise, a hum of approval, as though Apollo had simply played a particularly difficult chord on a piano.
"Come on," Rex wheezed.
His voice was a ruined rasp; Apollo had landed a blow square across his throat moments earlier, crushing the larynx before the regeneration could rebuild the cartilage.
"That’s it...?
Harder than that!"
Rex spat a glob of blood onto the shattered floor and leaned forward, his eyes bright with a terrifying, manic hunger.
"I know you’ve got more hatred stored in there, Apollo."
"I can feel it pulsing...
I put most of it there myself when I broke you."
The mockery in his tone was razor sharp, cutting through the divine fury like a poisoned blade.
Apollo’s reaction was primal.
His face contorted, the red light in his eyes bleeding outward until his entire head seemed to be composed of nothing but burning rage.
He didn’t speak and he didn’t roar.
He simply became motion.
He hit Rex again.
And then he did not stop.

chapters.title: Chapter 1175. I Offered Myself as a Sacrificial Lamb to My Own Curiosity
paragraphs: The beating that followed was not a fight; it was a systematic dismantling. For five agonizing minutes, Rex Rexilion endured a level of one-sided, relentless violence that he hadn’t experienced since the moment his own heart had stopped beating during his first death.
The world became nothing but a strobe light of crimson pain and the wet, nauseating sounds of impact.
Apollo had abandoned all pretense of martial arts. The Academy training, the measured breathing, and the tactical positioning it had all evaporated, consumed by a furnace of pure, unadulterated rage.
He wasn’t fighting Rex anymore; he was simply erasing him. His fists descended in an unbroken, mechanical rhythm, each strike carrying the weight of a collapsing star.
THUD CRUNCH.
THUD CRUNCH.
THUD CRUNCH.
Every time Apollo’s fist connected, Rex’s body was hammered into the domain floor like a spike being driven into wood.

The fractures spread outward in overlapping, spiderweb patterns across a fifty-meter radius. Whole sections of the pulsing violet surface began to flicker and die, the domain’s magical integrity hemorrhaging as Apollo’s power tore holes in the fabric of reality itself.

Blood was no longer something Rex coughed up; it was something he wore. It flowed freely from a shattered nose, leaked from his parted lips, and poured from a ragged gash above his left eye that refused to seal.
For the first time in two lifetimes, Infinite Regeneration, the absolute constant of Rex’s existence, was visibly failing to keep pace.
The wounds were being opened faster than the cellular knitting could close them. His body was a roadmap of fresh trauma, a mosaic of purple bruises, blackened burns, and split flesh.
After the first minute, a horrific new cadence emerged. It wasn’t the frenzy of a berserker; it was the methodical rhythm of an executioner.
Apollo would seize Rex by the collar of his coat, yank his broken form upright, and unleash four or five devastating blows to his face in rapid succession.
CRACK SPLASH.
Then, with contemptuous strength, Apollo would hurl him. Rex would become a ragdoll, hurtling through the air to crash into the darkness beyond the immediate circle of light.
But before Rex could even stagger to his hands and knees, coughing up chunks of lung tissue and saliva, Apollo would already be there.
The red gold energy wasn’t just powering his strikes; it was propelling him across the distance in instantaneous, blurring leaps that defied Rex’s ability to track.
Rex couldn’t commit to a full read he couldn’t afford to because by the time his brain processed Apollo’s trajectory, the fist was already connecting.

The domain itself seemed to recoil from the violence. Each iteration of the cycle left behind another patch of dead floor, a silent, dark crater where the violet pulse had been permanently extinguished.
SHRAKK BOOM!
In one particularly brutal moment, Apollo grabbed Rex with both hands, interlacing his fingers like a guillotine, and drove him downward with terrifying force.
Rex didn’t just hit the floor; he was buried a full meter deep into the stone.
Silence fell over the crater for a heartbeat, broken only by the ragged, wet gasps of the two combatants.
Apollo stood over the hole, his chest heaving, his entire body wreathed in a corona of murderous light. Steam rose from his skin where the heat of his power met the cooling air.
With a snarl of disgust, he reached down, fist clenching into Rex’s hair, and violently hauled him back up to eye level.
Rex’s head lolled back, his face a mask of crimson gore, his eyes half-lidded and unfocused.
"Say something else," Apollo hissed, his voice cracking with the strain of his fury.
The dual registers sounded like grinding metal. "You’ve had a great deal to say for the last hour...
"You’ve mocked me, analyzed me, dissected me!"
"Say something now, Rex!"
"Say something while you still have a tongue!"
Rex’s throat worked convulsively as he swallowed a mouthful of blood. A slow, terrifyingly calm smile spread across his ruined features.
Even with his skull fractured and his ribs grinding against one another, the defiance in his eyes remained unquenchable.
"Your left hook drops," Rex croaked, blood streaming down his chin in a steady rivulet.
He didn’t flinch from Apollo’s grip; instead, he leaned closer, his grin widening. "You’re carrying your weight too far forward on it."
"You’re overcompensating for the burn."
Rex’s eyes gleamed with a manic, predatory intelligence. "If I were actually trying, Apollo... if I stopped playing with you..."
"I would have taken your arm off at the shoulder four exchanges ago."
Apollo didn’t answer with words. He answered with the wet, grinding crunch of bone meeting divine fury.
His fist connected squarely with Rex’s jaw, the impact so violent that the mandible shattered into three distinct pieces before Rex’s head could even snap sideways.
CRUNCH SQUELCH.
But instead of a scream of agony, there came something far more unsettling: a laugh. It was a wet, broken sound—the noise of air escaping through shattered bone and blood-filled lungs.

Rex laughed through the fracture, the sound echoing unnaturally in the dying domain. His Infinite Regeneration struggled to compensate, the magical knitting process stuttering as it attempted to repair the jawbone while Rex’s own muscles were still spasming in the throes of a hysterical mirth.
It took nearly six agonizing seconds for the bone to reestablish its structure around the continuing laughter.

Deep within the neural pathways of his consciousness, Rex’s analytical mind remained terrifyingly detached. Somewhere around the third minute of this relentless torment, he had performed a genuine assessment.
He wasn’t calculating his chances of winning; he was calculating the limits of his own existence.

’Interesting,’ Rex thought, his inner monologue cool and clinical even as his vision swam in crimson. ’If this escalation continues... if his output scales exponentially with his rage, there is a non-zero probability that he will eventually produce enough destructive energy to vaporize my cellular structure faster than Infinite Regeneration can rebuild it.’
’He could literally outpace my immortality.
It was a slim probability. A sliver of mathematical doubt.
But it was not zero.
That number, that terrifying, beautiful number, was something he hadn’t seen attached to his own survival since the day he had purchased Avatar Creation.
The novelty of true mortality was almost... pleasant. It made the pain feel real. It made the fight feel like it mattered.
So, he let the beating continue. He offered himself up as a sacrificial lamb to his own curiosity.
THUD. CRACK. SPLAT.
Every impact was not merely trauma; it was data. Every broken rib, every ruptured organ, and every scorched patch of flesh fed his Adaptation ability.
He was touching a mechanism that defied every known taxonomy of magic in the world. He was sampling the divine.
[Analysis windows: 7 seconds... 5 seconds... 4.2 seconds...]
He could feel the coverage building. The system was no longer just reacting to individual strikes; it was beginning to map the underlying grammar of Apollo’s transformed state.
He was learning the language of a god through the medium of his own agony. Another four or five minutes of this, another few dozen shattered bones and hemorrhaged organs, and he would own it.
He would walk out of this collapsing hellscape with a capability the Apostle of Life had invented, only to have Rex steal it permanently.
’That is worth a broken face,’ Rex thought as his vision flickered. ’It is worth a dozen broken faces.’
’Give me more.’
Then came the final stretch. The descent into true hell.
Apollo stopped throwing him, and the distance was gone. The rage had become too focused, too intimate.
Now, Apollo held him. One fist was locked like a vise into the front of Rex’s coat, anchoring him in place, while the other fist became a piston of pure destruction.
WHAM. WHAM. WHAM. WHAM.

The sound filled the failing domain with a terrible, steady regularity. The empty space around them no longer absorbed the noise; the acoustics of the crumbling reality seemed to amplify every wet slap of flesh and every splintering crack of bone.

Rex’s head became a pendulum of pain, snapping back with each impact only to be hurled forward again to meet the next one. His healing was failing catastrophically; his features were no longer fully reassembling before the next strike tore them apart again.
He was caught in a perpetual cycle of being destroyed and partially rebuilt, a marionette of meat and bone.
SHLICK.
Somewhere in the chaos, his left eye socket collapsed. The orb ruptured, vision plunging into darkness on one side.
For two seconds, there was only blackness.
Then, the regeneration dragged the eye back into alignment.
CRUNCH.
Then came the worst of it. His left cheekbone and orbital bone both disintegrated under a concentrated burst of divine pressure.
For nine agonizing seconds, there was simply a gaping hole in the side of his face, a raw crater of exposed muscle and teeth where his skeletal structure should have been.
Nine seconds—the longest single interval Infinite Regeneration had ever failed to close a wound.
In those nine seconds of raw, exposed vulnerability, Rex didn’t scream. He didn’t beg.
Even as his brain teetered on the edge of shock, and even as the blood loss threatened to drag him into the abyss, he kept talking.
Between the blows, through the blood and the broken bone, the mockery remained.

chapters.title: Chapter 1176. I Wasn’t Being Beaten, I Was Being Worshipped by My Own Design
paragraphs: Rex’s words came out as a wet, gurgling slurry, his tongue struggling to navigate a mouth that had become a ruined landscape of torn flesh and shattered enamel.

Yet, despite the agony, despite the way his brain screamed at him to shut up and die, he pushed forward. He wanted to twist the knife in Apollo’s psyche as deeply as Apollo was twisting the knife in his body.
"You know what I like about this?" Rex wheezed.
The words were punctuated by crimson bubbles escaping his lips. "It’s... it’s the first honest thing you’ve done all year."
WHAM.
Apollo’s fist connected with Rex’s sternum, the shockwave so immense that the energy rippled through the domain floor like a physical wave, spiderwebbing a section of stone forty meters away.
CRACK THOOM.
Rex’s lungs seized, air whistling through a punctured pleura, but he forced the next words out. "Everything else you do... you do because you think you’re supposed to."
"The heroics. The martyrdom. Protecting the city. Leading the network. Standing up in front of four thousand people and telling them they’re fighting for something noble."

Rex coughed, and a molar clattered onto the cracked floor, spinning like a die before coming to rest in a pool of blood. Before the tooth had even stopped bouncing, Rex felt the sickening, itchy pressure of the replacement already pushing through his bleeding gums.
"This is the first time... I’ve seen you do something... because you actually want to."
Apollo’s entire body stiffened. The red gold corona around him flared with such intensity that the air itself seemed to combust.
He stopped mid-strike, holding Rex aloft by the ruined collar of his coat. His breathing wasn’t labored anymore; it was steady, cold, and terrifying.
"Don’t," Apollo said.

His voice had dropped to a quiet, hollow register that was infinitely worse than his earlier screaming. It was the sound of a man who had moved past anger into something far more dangerous: absolute conviction.
"Don’t tell me what I want."
"But it’s true." Rex’s grin returned.

It was a grotesque sight, a mask of gore stretched over a skull that was barely holding together, but the mockery in those bloodshot eyes was unmistakable. "You’ve spent your whole life carrying a role like it was armor, Apollo..."
"You wore that morality like a cage, and you never once asked whether the person underneath actually agreed with it."
Rex leaned into the fist that was pressed against his throat, savoring the burn. "And now?"
"Now you’re finally, genuinely doing what you want instead of what a ’good man’ would do.
"And the only reason you finally found yourself is because I took everything else out of your way."
Rex let out a laugh. It was a wet, rattling sound that tore at his throat, each syllable sending fresh waves of agony through his shattered ribcage.
"You should thank me... Honestly... I gave you the first authentic moment of your entire life."
For three seconds, there was absolute silence. Then, the dam broke.
"DO YOU THINK I’M AFRAID TO KILL YOU?" Apollo roared.
His voice had completely transformed. The human timbre was gone, replaced entirely by that terrifying, doubled dark register, a sound that resonated not in the ears but in the marrow of the bones.
It was the sound of something ancient and merciless.
SHLICK CRUNCH! SHLICK CRUNCH! SHLICK CRUNCH!
Apollo grabbed Rex by the front of his coat with one hand, yanking him off the ground so his toes scraped uselessly against the debris, and unleashed hell with the other.

Each strike was a piston of divine wrath, each fist wreathed in that unstable, crimson gold energy that burned as it broke. He wasn’t just hitting Rex; he was trying to pulverize him out of existence.
BOOM. CRUNCH. SPLAT.

Blood sprayed across Apollo’s face, painting his divine features in a macabre crimson. The impacts were so fast they became a continuous, wet percussion that drowned out the crumbling sounds of the domain.

"I AM GOING TO TEAR EVERY INCH OF YOU APART!" Apollo screamed, each word punctuated by a blow that could have leveled a fortress. "I WILL TEAR YOU DOWN UNTIL THERE ISN’T ENOUGH LEFT FOR ANYTHING TO REGENERATE!"
"I WILL LEAVE NOTHING BUT DUST AND MEMORY!"
Rex laughed. It was a sound that defied biology: a wet, bubbling gurgle that erupted from a chest cavity filled with blood and lungs that felt like they were being shredded by broken glass.

His face was a grotesque ruin. The left side of his skull was a sagging crater where the cheekbone had been pulverized, the bone fragments struggling to knit back together beneath a flap of torn muscle.
His left eye was a swollen, purple slit, half buried behind a ridge of inflamed tissue. Yet, through the carnage, he grinned a wide, crimson smile that stretched the raw edges of his wounds.
He looked less like a man and more like a demon that had been torn apart only to find the experience amusing.
WHAM. CRACK. SPLAT.
The onslaught continued, each of Apollo’s strikes carrying the force of a meteor impact. But Rex was not fighting back.
Not even close.

In the cold, silent sanctum of his mind, Rex watched the data streams. He could have ended this farce in seconds. If he unleashed even a fraction of his true potential, the fight would have been over before Apollo could blink.
Gravity Manipulation, applied with ruthless precision, would have increased the pressure on Apollo’s body by a hundredfold, crushing him into a flat smear of divine flesh against the domain floor.
The Temporal Authority embedded in his soul register could have frozen time itself, suspending Apollo in a static moment of rage while Rex calmly dismantled him piece by piece.
But he held back. He restrained the god-slaying power coiled in his veins for two distinct, equally selfish reasons.
First, there was the tactical necessity. His Adaptation ability was screaming with hunger.

Every time Apollo’s red gold fist connected, every time that alien, divine energy burned through his flesh, Rex’s system ingested the data. His analytical windows were closing faster and faster, and the comprehension was nearly complete.
He needed the contact. He needed the pain.
He needed to experience the full spectrum of Apollo’s wrath to truly own it. He wanted that coverage more than he wanted his own safety.
Second, there was something darker. Something more primal.

For eighteen months, Rex had been an architect of destruction. He had meticulously studied Apollo, learned his triggers, mapped his morality, and systematically dismantled every pillar of his identity.
He had built this rage with more patience and care than he had put into any other project in either of his lives. He had cultivated this hatred like a gardener tends to a poisonous flower.
And now, sitting in the middle of the storm he had created, he felt an enormous, uncomplicated pleasure. Being on the receiving end of Apollo’s murderous fury was the ultimate validation.
The rage pouring out of Apollo was the proof that Rex’s work had been flawless. He wasn’t just being beaten; he was being worshipped by the very hatred he had engineered.
CRUNCH.

Apollo’s fist buried itself into Rex’s ribs, sending fresh sprays of arterial blood across the violet floor. Rex’s body convulsed, but his eyes remained locked on Apollo’s, bright with a terrifying, lucid satisfaction.
"You can’t kill me," Rex said.

The words were mangled, forced through a mouth that was more wound than flesh, each syllable accompanied by a spray of crimson. His voice was hoarse, wrecked by the blood filling his throat, but the conviction behind it was absolute.
It was the voice of something that had moved beyond the concept of death.

"No matter how hard you try, Apollo," Rex continued, his laughter breaking through the blood again, wet and mocking. "No matter how many bones you shatter... no matter how much of me you spill across this floor... it won’t matter."
He leaned forward as much as his broken body would allow, his bloodied face inches from Apollo’s divine fury.
"I can’t die," Rex whispered through the gore, his grin widening impossibly. "Not anymore..."
"Not the way you’re thinking about it..."
"You’re trying to kill a man, Apollo... but you’re only breaking a vessel."
