The impacts were so fast they became a continuous, wet percussion that drowned out the crumbling sounds of the domain.
"I AM GOING TO TEAR EVERY INCH OF YOU APART!" Apollo screamed, each word punctuated by a blow that could have leveled a fortress.
"I WILL TEAR YOU DOWN UNTIL THERE ISN’T ENOUGH LEFT FOR ANYTHING TO REGENERATE!"
"I WILL LEAVE NOTHING BUT DUST AND MEMORY!"
Rex laughed.
It was a sound that defied biology: a wet, bubbling gurgle that erupted from a chest cavity filled with blood and lungs that felt like they were being shredded by broken glass.
His face was a grotesque ruin.
The left side of his skull was a sagging crater where the cheekbone had been pulverized, the bone fragments struggling to knit back together beneath a flap of torn muscle.
His left eye was a swollen, purple slit, half buried behind a ridge of inflamed tissue.
Yet, through the carnage, he grinned a wide, crimson smile that stretched the raw edges of his wounds.
He looked less like a man and more like a demon that had been torn apart only to find the experience amusing.
WHAM.
CRACK.
SPLAT.
The onslaught continued, each of Apollo’s strikes carrying the force of a meteor impact.
But Rex was not fighting back.
Not even close.
In the cold, silent sanctum of his mind, Rex watched the data streams.
He could have ended this farce in seconds.
If he unleashed even a fraction of his true potential, the fight would have been over before Apollo could blink.
Gravity Manipulation, applied with ruthless precision, would have increased the pressure on Apollo’s body by a hundredfold, crushing him into a flat smear of divine flesh against the domain floor.
The Temporal Authority embedded in his soul register could have frozen time itself, suspending Apollo in a static moment of rage while Rex calmly dismantled him piece by piece.
But he held back.
He restrained the god-slaying power coiled in his veins for two distinct, equally selfish reasons.
First, there was the tactical necessity.
His Adaptation ability was screaming with hunger.
Every time Apollo’s red gold fist connected, every time that alien, divine energy burned through his flesh, Rex’s system ingested the data.
His analytical windows were closing faster and faster, and the comprehension was nearly complete.
He needed the contact.
He needed the pain.
He needed to experience the full spectrum of Apollo’s wrath to truly own it.
He wanted that coverage more than he wanted his own safety.
Second, there was something darker.
Something more primal.
For eighteen months, Rex had been an architect of destruction.
He had meticulously studied Apollo, learned his triggers, mapped his morality, and systematically dismantled every pillar of his identity.
He had built this rage with more patience and care than he had put into any other project in either of his lives.
He had cultivated this hatred like a gardener tends to a poisonous flower.
And now, sitting in the middle of the storm he had created, he felt an enormous, uncomplicated pleasure.
Being on the receiving end of Apollo’s murderous fury was the ultimate validation.
The rage pouring out of Apollo was the proof that Rex’s work had been flawless.
He wasn’t just being beaten; he was being worshipped by the very hatred he had engineered.
CRUNCH.
Apollo’s fist buried itself into Rex’s ribs, sending fresh sprays of arterial blood across the violet floor.
Rex’s body convulsed, but his eyes remained locked on Apollo’s, bright with a terrifying, lucid satisfaction.
"You can’t kill me," Rex said.
The words were mangled, forced through a mouth that was more wound than flesh, each syllable accompanied by a spray of crimson.
His voice was hoarse, wrecked by the blood filling his throat, but the conviction behind it was absolute.
It was the voice of something that had moved beyond the concept of death.
"No matter how hard you try, Apollo," Rex continued, his laughter breaking through the blood again, wet and mocking.
"No matter how many bones you shatter... no matter how much of me you spill across this floor... it won’t matter."
He leaned forward as much as his broken body would allow, his bloodied face inches from Apollo’s divine fury.
"I can’t die," Rex whispered through the gore, his grin widening impossibly.
"Not anymore..."
"Not the way you’re thinking about it..."
"You’re trying to kill a man, Apollo... but you’re only breaking a vessel."

chapters.title: Chapter 1177. You’re Fighting a War Against a Ghost That Can Wear Flesh
paragraphs: The world seemed to stutter.
Apollo froze. His fist was already drawn back, coiled like a serpent ready to strike, suspended at the apex of its arc.
The divine energy crackling around his knuckles screamed in the sudden silence, a high-pitched whine that vibrated through the very atoms of the domain.
His chest heaved, each breath a ragged tear in the air, and the iron tight grip he held on Rex’s ruined coat slackened by a fraction, not out of mercy, but out of sheer, stunned disbelief.
The red gold corona surrounding him pulsed once, violently, like a dying star, before holding steady in a low, ominous glow. Apollo’s eyes, burning with a light that was no longer human, narrowed.

Suspicion flickered across his features, but it didn’t last; it quickly soured into something far more primal and ugly. It was the look of a predator that had realized its prey wasn’t just refusing to run; it was enjoying the hunt.
"What does that mean?" Apollo asked.
His voice was barely a whisper, but it carried more weight than the thunderous roars from before. It was quiet, precise, and lethally dangerous.
Rex didn’t flinch. He didn’t even blink.
With a wet, grinding sound, he turned his head to the side, dislodging a thick clot of blood that had been pooling in his cheek. He spat the crimson mass onto the cracked floor.
Ptu!

And watched it splatter against the stone before meeting Apollo’s gaze with terrifying clarity. His features were a horrific mosaic of trauma; the bone fragments were already grinding against each other as they reassembled, the flesh knitting with an audible, sickening squelch.
"It means," Rex answered, the grin splitting his blood-slicked face wider, "that you can break this body into as many pieces as you want."
"Go ahead... Burn it... Crush it!"
"Tear it apart until there’s nothing left but a red smear across this floor."
A wet chuckle escaped his throat. "It will never be enough to actually end me, Apollo."
"Not this body. Not any body you can reach."
"You’re fighting a war against a ghost that can wear flesh whenever it pleases."
For a heartbeat, the tension between them was so absolute it felt as though reality itself might snap. Apollo didn’t argue.
He didn’t lecture. He didn’t invoke justice or morality.

All of those things—the hero, the leader, and the protector—had been burned away in the furnace of Rex’s provocation. The man who had stood before four thousand soldiers that morning was dead; something singular and terrifying now stood in his place.
The last vestiges of Apollo’s humanity collapsed. There was no calculation left in his eyes, no consideration for collateral damage or the sanctity of life.
The divine fury had crystallized into a single, razor-sharp purpose: the complete and utter annihilation of the thing standing before him. He wasn’t trying to win anymore; he was trying to erase.
Slowly, deliberately, Apollo drew his fist back even further. The air around his arm began to distort, warped by the sheer density of the energy gathering there.

The red gold light intensified until it was blinding, casting long, demonic shadows across the dying domain. The sound of the energy gathering resembled the grinding of tectonic plates, accompanied by a RUMBLE and CRACKLE.
His face was a mask of divine hatred, cold and absolute.
"Let’s find out," Apollo said.
The strike did not just land; it detonated.
Apollo unleashed every remaining fragment of his existence.

The rage that had been simmering for months, the hatred that had been meticulously harvested by Rex, and the last, dying embers of the goddess’s borrowed light were all compressed into a single, impossible point of singularity.
His fist became the epicenter of a collapsing star.
BOOM!!!
When his knuckles connected with the center of Rex’s sternum, the sound wasn’t a punch; it was a sonic boom that shattered the silence of the domain.

The impact cratered the floor instantly, sending shockwaves rippling outward in twenty-meter concentric circles of pulverized stone and displaced air. The domain itself screamed in protest; the unanchored structure groaned as the violet pulse of the reality around them began to fail.

Whole sections of the horizon flickered like a dying fluorescent bulb, and the fabric of spacetime began to tear, leaving jagged, black wounds hanging open in the air where reality simply ceased to exist.

Rex’s body didn’t just fall; it was launched. The force of the blow sent him hurtling across the full length of the domain, a broken projectile tumbling end over end through the strobing, failing light.
He became a blur of crimson and shadow, crashing through debris before disappearing into the far reaches of the abyss where the floor had long since dissolved into nothingness.
The silence that followed was immediate, heavy, and suffocating.
Then, the sound began.
It started as a faint echo, bouncing off the crumbling walls and the fracturing sky. But as it traveled across the enormous distance of the ruined space, it grew louder, clearer, and more terrifying.
It was laughter.
Apollo stood alone in the epicenter of the devastation. His fist remained extended, his arm locked in place by the sheer aftershock of the blow.

His chest heaved in violent, ragged spasms, each breath tasting like copper and burnt ozone. He stood frozen as the laughter reverberated through the hollow bones of his own body, echoing off the surfaces that were coming apart at the seams.
Ha... Hahaha... AH HA HA HA!
He listened. He listened while the red gold corona around him pulsed erratically, struggling to maintain its form.

He listened while sections of the violet floor died in widening patches around his feet, plunging the world into a terrifying twilight. He listened as the very foundation of the space groaned like a dying beast somewhere in the distant dark.
And in that moment, with a clarity that felt like a blade sliding between his ribs, Apollo understood. He understood the horror of his situation.
The man he had just struck with the full measure of his divine wrath—the man he had tried to erase from existence—was not only still alive out there in the dark, but he was happy.
The laughter wasn’t the sound of a victim. It was the sound of a connoisseur who had just tasted something exquisite.
"I’m not going to stop," Apollo said.
His voice was hollow, directed at no one. He spoke to the darkness, to the void, to whatever pathetic remains of his own soul were still clinging to consciousness.
"I will not stop."
But the laughter did not cease.
It went on.
And on.
And on...

It was genuinely delighted, unforced, rich, and terrifyingly sincere. It was the sound of a man experiencing a moment of pure, unadulterated joy, more profound than anything he had felt in either of his lives.
And beneath the mirth, there was something worse than fear: there was a calm, unshakable certainty.

The laughter carried a message that echoed louder than any shout: regardless of what Apollo Brightsoul did next, no matter how far he descended into darkness, no matter how much of his humanity he burned away to fuel his vengeance... it would never, ever be enough.

chapters.title: Chapter 1178. It Was an Insult to Death Itself
paragraphs: The echo of the final punch did not merely fade; it convulsed. It rolled through the domain in overlapping waves of displaced air, bouncing off impossible geometries that should not have produced sound at all.

Beneath that dying rumble, the great fissure splitting the pulsing violet floor screamed in silence, spiderwebbing outward in slow, deliberate branches less like breaking stone and more like a malignant organism claiming territory.
Rex lay entombed in the center of the wreckage his own momentum had carved. What remained of him was a grotesque parody of human anatomy.
Through a jagged tear in his shirt, the pale, splintered edge of a rib punched outward through the skin, white and obscene against the crimson ruin of his chest.

Blood didn’t merely trickle from his mouth; it flowed in a steady, rhythmic pulse, pooling beneath his jaw and spreading across the violet surface in a dark, viscous stain that refused to be absorbed, sitting atop the floor like spilled oil.
His left arm lay twisted at an impossible angle, the radius and ulna having snapped beneath the skin to create a sickening bulge that defied every natural joint.
Crack.
A wet, grinding sound erupted from the center of the carnage.

Underneath the carnage, quieter now but infinitely more terrifying, the sound persisted. It had softened from the full, unrestrained bark of earlier into something more primal, a series of ragged, wet exhales.
Each breath was a battle against the copper tide rising in his throat, forcing blood to bubble past his lips in a frothy crimson foam.
Hhhhk grah hhhk.
rhythm was mechanical, relentless, and utterly wrong.

Apollo Brightsoul stood frozen, his own chest heaving, the magical residue of his last spell still crackling like dying embers around his fingertips. His eyes were locked on that twitching, broken form.
’Why won’t he just stay down?’ Apollo thought, his pulse hammering against his eardrums like a war drum. ’I felt the bone shatter...’
’I felt the impact liquefy the organs...’
’By every law of flesh and spirit, he should be meat...’
’So why is he still breathing?’
A droplet of sweat rolled down Apollo’s temple, stinging his eye, but he couldn’t blink. He couldn’t move.
The tension in the air was so thick it felt like breathing mercury. Every time Rex’s lungs wheezed, the violet floor seemed to shudder in sympathy.
"Finish it," Apollo whispered, his voice cracking, barely audible over the wet rasp of Rex’s breathing. "Just die, damn you."
But Rex didn’t die. Instead, a clawed hand’s fingernails, torn to bloody stumps, scraped against the violet stone.
Skreeeeee.
The sound set Apollo’s teeth on edge. The broken man’s fingers curled, seeking purchase in the cracks of the domain.
Shhhhh, tchk.

The sound of grinding bone shifting inside Rex’s mangled arm echoed through the void. Rex’s head lolled to the side, eyes unfocused and bloodshot, staring at nothing, yet his body seemed to be coiled like a spring made of broken glass.
The sheer stubbornness of his survival was more violent than any spell Apollo had cast. It was an insult to death itself.

Apollo’s fingers began to glow again, not with the controlled elegance of his earlier magic, but with a desperate, flickering desperation. The air began to hum with static, the violet floor reacting to the spike in his volatile mana.
"I’ll break what’s left," Apollo hissed through clenched teeth, his knuckles whitening as he prepared to unleash another torrent of celestial energy. "I’ll grind you into dust."
Yet, even as he prepared the strike, Apollo’s inner mind screamed a warning. The rhythm of Rex’s breathing hadn’t changed.
It wasn’t the sound of a dying man clinging to life; it was the sound of a predator waiting for the moment to snap.

Far above the carnage of the domain, suspended in a corridor that neither man occupied anymore, the war bled on a mindless, grinding machine of meat and metal that continued its work without regard for the two titans fighting in the void below.

The sudden disappearance of Apollo Brightsoul and the masked figure had carved a disorienting wound into the center of the battlefield. It was a tactical vacuum, a hole in the shape of two legendary combatants that left both armies staggering like drunkards in a storm.
On the Aethelgard side, the chain of command didn’t just fracture; it shattered.
"Press the advantage!" shrieked Commander Valerius, his face flushed crimson with desperation. "They’re gone!"
"Their leadership has evaporated!"
"Hold the line, you fool!" another commander roared back, the sound of steel clashing against steel punctuating his rage. "We cannot advance without knowing where the enemy’s reserves lie!"
"Someone make a fucking call!" a third screamed, his voice cracking as he watched his soldiers hesitate, trapped between the terror of the unknown and the instinct to attack.

In the chaos of this indecision, Captain Dessin Farrow saw not opportunity but a chance to salvage his honor. His heart hammered against his ribs. "Thisthis is it," the moment where we break them, and he made the call that would haunt the survivors.
"Forward! For Aethelgard!"
"Close the gap!" Farrow bellowed, drawing his blade. "Push into the space where Xerollion stood! Now!"

Forty soldiers, driven by a cocktail of adrenaline and false hope, surged forward. They charged into the empty space where the Underlayer’s leader had stood moments before, their boots thundering against the stone.
They covered fifteen meters before the trap snapped shut.
It wasn’t a collapse; it was a surgical strike.
Gorvasha’s reserve formation didn’t panic; they flowed. Like black mercury pouring into a crack, her forces folded around Farrow’s advancing line from both flanks.
The maneuver was so precise, so devastatingly smooth, that it felt as though the Underlayer had been rehearsing this exact slaughter since the moment the fighting resumed.
CRUNCH.
The wet slap of steel meeting flesh drowned out the sound of breaking bones. The advance was slaughtered in seconds.

Twenty-two of the forty men were butchered where they stood, their screams cut short by crossbow bolts and the vicious sweep of demonic blades. Farrow himself felt the wind of a massive axe as it whistled toward his skull. Sssshhhhk, but he only survived because a private, a girl barely twenty who had been trembling moments before, threw herself bodily into the path of the blade.
The axe bit deep into her shoulder, the sound of her clavicle snapping echoing like a dry branch breaking, but she died buying him three seconds of life.
"Fall back!" Farrow screamed, but there was no one left to follow.
The gap had become a grave.
On the Underlayer side, however, the chaos was nonexistent. There was no hesitation, no panicked shouting, only the cold, terrifying precision of practiced violence.
Cassandra Vexmoor stepped into the vacuum left by the violet spiral the instant it closed. Her presence was like an anchor in a hurricane.
When she spoke, her voice didn’t need to carry; it commanded the very air to still.
"Hold the kill zone formation," she commanded.
Her tone was flat, devoid of emotion, carrying the absolute authority of someone who had commanded legions long before these men drew their first breath. "Nobody breaks position!"
"Not one step forward, not one step back."
The soldiers around her froze mid-motion, their blades lowering to hold the defensive posture.
"He will be back," Cassandra continued, her eyes fixed on the spot where the dimension had torn open, "and when he returns, this corridor needs to look exactly the way he left it."
"We do not waste blood on lesser prey."
A few hundred yards down the line, Gorvasha mirrored the discipline.
"Hold formation!" she barked to her own section, her massive warhammer already mid-swing.
WHAM.
The hammer connected with an Aethelgard soldier’s chest cavity, sending ribs splintering outward in a spray of crimson as she repelled another desperate advance.

The confusion that had briefly threatened to paralyze the demon ranks had been severed cleanly by the two women at the helm. As the Aethelgard forces recoiled from the slaughter Farrow had invited, the corridor’s defensive structure held firm.
The Underlayer’s line remained unbroken, a wall of iron and malice waiting patiently for the storm to return.

Twenty-two of the forty men were butchered where they stood, their screams cut short by crossbow bolts and the vicious sweep of demonic blades.
Farrow himself felt the wind of a massive axe as it whistled toward his skull.
Sssshhhhk, but he only survived because a private, a girl barely twenty who had been trembling moments before, threw herself bodily into the path of the blade.
The axe bit deep into her shoulder, the sound of her clavicle snapping echoing like a dry branch breaking, but she died buying him three seconds of life.
"Fall back!" Farrow screamed, but there was no one left to follow.
The gap had become a grave.
On the Underlayer side, however, the chaos was nonexistent.
There was no hesitation, no panicked shouting, only the cold, terrifying precision of practiced violence.
Cassandra Vexmoor stepped into the vacuum left by the violet spiral the instant it closed.
Her presence was like an anchor in a hurricane.
When she spoke, her voice didn’t need to carry; it commanded the very air to still.
"Hold the kill zone formation," she commanded.
Her tone was flat, devoid of emotion, carrying the absolute authority of someone who had commanded legions long before these men drew their first breath.
"Nobody breaks position!"
"Not one step forward, not one step back."
The soldiers around her froze mid-motion, their blades lowering to hold the defensive posture.
"He will be back," Cassandra continued, her eyes fixed on the spot where the dimension had torn open, "and when he returns, this corridor needs to look exactly the way he left it."
"We do not waste blood on lesser prey."
A few hundred yards down the line, Gorvasha mirrored the discipline.
"Hold formation!" she barked to her own section, her massive warhammer already mid-swing.
WHAM.
The hammer connected with an Aethelgard soldier’s chest cavity, sending ribs splintering outward in a spray of crimson as she repelled another desperate advance.
The confusion that had briefly threatened to paralyze the demon ranks had been severed cleanly by the two women at the helm.
As the Aethelgard forces recoiled from the slaughter Farrow had invited, the corridor’s defensive structure held firm.
The Underlayer’s line remained unbroken, a wall of iron and malice waiting patiently for the storm to return.

chapters.title: Chapter 1179. I Rehearsed Grief a Dozen Times Before It Ever Mattered
paragraphs: Elliot Von Starlight was fighting like a man walking through a dream or a nightmare. His blade moved with automatic precision, but his soul was fractured, scattered across the distance between the physical world and the void where his friend had been swallowed.

He pulled his sword arm back three separate times in mid-swing, the motion stuttering like a broken machine. His eyes kept drifting, drawn like moths to a flame, toward that empty, mocking patch of corridor where Apollo had vanished.
The lapse was nearly fatal. Twice, the cold bite of a demon’s blade had whistled toward his carotid artery, the steel mere millimeters from opening his throat before a flash of silver intervened.
Clang!
Evelyn appeared between them, her blade intercepting the demon’s axe with such force that sparks showered Elliot’s face. She didn’t scold him, and she didn’t shout.
There was no room for reprimand in the middle of a slaughter. She simply positioned herself in the gap his distraction left behind, a living shield between him and death.
But even her legendary focus was fraying; every few seconds, her gaze would betray her, darting involuntarily toward that hollow stretch of stone.
"He’ll be fine," Elliot gritted out, the words tasting like copper and desperation. "He has to be fine..."
"He’s Apollo... the Apostle of Life..."
To emphasize the words, he pivoted on his heel and drove his sword into an advancing orc’s shield with the full weight of his fury.
CRACK SHATTER.

The reinforced wood exploded into splinters, but the force didn’t stop there; the shockwave traveled up the arm of the demon, snapping the radius and ulna with a wet, grinding pop that echoed through the immediate chaos.
The orc screamed as its shattered limb hung uselessly by tendons, but Elliot was already moving past, his mind already gone again.
Evelyn said nothing.
How could she?

She had spent the last hour witnessing two beings tear apart the fabric of reality. Reassurance felt like a currency she had spent entirely during those first few minutes of the clash; she had none left to give.
A few hundred meters back, Valentina held her section of the retreat corridor with a disciplined economy that bordered on the supernatural. But her tactical mind was hemorrhaging focus.

Her eyes kept snapping to that empty void. Twice she had already begun the mental calculations to redirect reinforcements toward the epicenter of the disappearance, only to halt herself with a bitter snarl.
There were no reinforcements to send. You couldn’t fortify a hole in existence.

’Stay sharp, Valentina,’ she commanded herself, her knuckles white around her weapon. ’Whatever crawls out of that gap, whether it’s Apollo returning or a catastrophe that ends us all, it’s going to need a solid line to hit.’
’If we break now, we die before the real threat even arrives.’
Meanwhile, Morwenna fought with a cold, mechanical discipline that refused to waver, yet her inner world was collapsing.

Her thoughts kept circling back to a memory she had buried deep: a quiet morning in her own bedroom, the sunlight filtering through the curtains, and a promise made about protecting her family’s honor.
She had walked into this corridor believing she understood the man she had bound herself to. She thought she knew his strength. She thought she knew his limits.

But watching that empty stretch of stone, where two titans had punched through the world itself, she felt a cold shiver of realization. Her understanding hadn’t just been flawed; it had been dangerously, catastrophically incomplete.
She wasn’t bound to a man; she was bound to something that defied the very concept of mortal boundaries.

And cutting through the blood-soaked front ranks with flawless, practiced competence, Rex Rexilion fought. He shouted commands, he parried blows, and he slaughtered anything that dared approach his position, but beneath the roar of battle, beneath the spray of arterial blood, and beneath the screams of the dying, Rex was worrying.
His every strike was laced with the frantic energy of a man who knew that the world was about to change forever.

Rex Rexilion moved through the slaughter like a demon wearing the skin of a hero. He was a whirlwind of steel and controlled fury, his blade carving through demon flesh with wet, tearing sounds shhhhk tchk as he severed limbs and opened throats.
But his performance was layered. To the soldiers of Aethelgard, he was the picture of desperate bravery.
He shouted encouragements that rang hollow with emotion, his voice cracking as he bellowed Apollo’s name toward that empty, mocking void.
"Apollo!" he roared, the sound laced with a raw, genuine-sounding terror that made nearby privates flinch. "Apollo, answer me!"

The soldiers around him saw it as the noble breakdown of a commander barely holding his sanity together. They saw a man fighting for his life while drowning in grief. Nobody questioned the cracks in his voice.
Nobody could. The performance required zero cognitive effort from Rex; he had rehearsed this exact routine of ’the grieving hero’ dozens of times over the past year.
He could weep for a lost friend while simultaneously calculating the optimal angle to sever a demon’s jugular without breaking his stride.
But inside the domain, there was no performance. There was only the grotesque reality of two broken gods.
Apollo Brightsoul stood over the wreckage, his chest heaving, his magical aura flickering like a dying star. His eyes were fixed on the mangled heap that was Rex Rexilion.
He couldn’t make sense of it. The physics of the fight had ended minutes ago, yet the sound that was wet and rhythmic rasping continued.
"Why are you still laughing?" Apollo demanded.
His voice broke, splintering between white-hot fury and a cold, creeping horror that made his skin crawl. "I just shattered your ribs!
"I felt them snap under my fist! You should be screaming in agony."
"You should be begging for death!"
A wet, gurgling sound rose from the crimson pool beneath Rex.
"I am in agony, Apollo." Rex’s voice was wrecked, each syllable dragged through a throat clogged with blood and bile.
But beneath the carnage, the terrifying calm remained unshaken. "The pain... it’s exquisite."
"I feel every splintered bone grinding against my lungs..."
"I feel the blood filling my chest..."
"But fear?" A wet chuckle escaped his lips. "Fear is something I stopped genuinely carrying a long time ago."
Apollo snapped. The last thread of his restraint burned away in a flash of celestial rage.

He dropped to his knees in the gore, his fingers clawing into the ruined front of Rex’s coat. With a guttural roar of effort, he hauled the broken body upward, dragging Rex up until their faces were inches apart.
Splat.
A thick glob of blood fell from Rex’s chin, landing directly onto Apollo’s white knuckled fist.
Apollo’s eyes were bloodshot, his pupils dilated with a rage that had transcended grief.
"You destroyed everything," Apollo hissed, his voice dropping to a lethal, vibrating register. "You burned my world to ash."
"You slaughtered the people I loved like they were nothing but livestock."
"You stole the hearts of everyone who dared to hope..."

"You laid your filthy hands on my own mother..." He shook Rex violently, the sound of grinding bone echoing in the small space. "...and you think you can sit here, broken and dying in my grip, and laugh like this is some twisted fucking joke?"
Rex didn’t flinch. Even as his body screamed in protest, even as his internal organs shifted with the motion, his eyes remained bright with a sickening, lucid intelligence.
The grin spread wider, splitting the blood-slicked skin of his cheeks, revealing teeth stained crimson.
"Because it is a joke, Apollo," Rex whispered, his breath smelling of copper and death. "All of this—this war, this pain, this pathetic struggle for meaning—it’s all just a performance."
"The finest one I have ever had the privilege to watch." His eyes locked onto Apollo’s with predatory intensity. "And you, Apollo... you have been its absolute star."

chapters.title: Chapter 1180. For the First Time, I Felt the Current Pulling at My Ankles
paragraphs: Apollo didn’t throw him with the practiced technique of a warrior; he discarded him like refuse. His fingers uncurled, releasing Rex’s mangled frame.
Rex’s body hit the cracked violet floor with a sickening, wet thud, the sound of shattered ribs grinding against stone and organs shifting uncomfortably in a ruined cavity.
Apollo stepped back. His chest heaved in ragged, violent spasms, but the tears had dried.

The raw, bleeding wound of his grief had cauterized itself in real time, leaving behind something far more terrifying: a cold, calcified resolve. The expression on his face had ceased to be human; the sorrow had been hollowed out, replaced by a terrifying, focused emptiness.
The energy surrounding him began to warp. The loose, blazing red gold aura that had been flaring outward like a dying sun began to retract.

It didn’t fade; it condensed. The light pulled inward, clinging to his skin like molten metal, forming a second skin of pressurized divinity that hummed with a low, subsonic frequency that made the very air vibrate.
Mmmmmmmmmmmmm.
"You said I was only the protagonist of a story that was never mine," Apollo said.
His voice had changed. The tremor was gone, replaced by a resonance so deep it felt as though it were vibrating through Rex’s own shattered bones.
The divine timbre beneath his words thickened, layered like ancient stone. "Fine... Then let me write the ending to yours."
The light began to climb.
This was not the warm, life-giving radiance of his earlier spells. That golden glow had been a gift, a tool of creation and protection.
What was manifesting now was different. It was purer.
It was colder. It was a bleached, terrifying white gold that seemed to suck the color out of the surrounding domain.

Rex, lying in the pooling crimson of his own blood, felt something he hadn’t experienced in decades: a lurch of genuine, visceral concern. His analytical mind, the one that had catalogued every limit of Apollo’s power, began to scream warnings.
’Impossible,’ Rex thought, his inner monologue fractured by the pain of a punctured lung. ’The four-minute ceiling...’
’The mana burn... The inevitable collapse of the mortal vessel...’
’He always hits the wall... He always breaks before the power does...’
But the wall was gone.
The four-minute limit that governed every version of Apollo’s power Rex had ever studied—every skirmish, every duel, and every catastrophic display—simply ceased to exist.
There was no countdown ticking down in the back of Apollo’s mind. There was no warning shiver of magical exhaustion.

Instead, there was only an open channel. A direct, unregulated torrent of power flowing from somewhere far beyond the celestial heavens, beyond mortal designation, pouring through Apollo’s body like water through a dam that had been completely demolished.

The light wasn’t just surrounding him now; it was consuming him, burning through his flesh and spirit without any apparent limit on duration, transforming the man into something that could only be described as a walking apocalypse.
"What... what are you doing?" Rex wheezed, a crimson bubble of blood popping on his lips as he stared up at the silhouette of a god.
Apollo didn’t answer with words. He simply raised his hand, and the space between them began to scream.

Somewhere beyond sound and physical vibration, Rex Rexilion sensed physical vibration; Rex Rexilion felt it as an adjustment in the fundamental pressure of reality. It wasn’t the arrival of a presence; it was the sudden, terrifying shift in the atmosphere that precedes a cataclysmic storm.
The air didn’t just feel heavier; it felt occupied.
With the cold, razor-sharp clarity that only surfaced when death was no longer a threat but an immediate certainty, Rex understood.
This was not the Goddess of Life acting as a passive observer, granting Apollo a trickle of healing light as she had earlier. This was different.

This was the Goddess choosing. She was deliberately, with full awareness of the mortal cost, authorizing a portion of her own divine essence to flood through a vessel she had judged worth the catastrophic risk.
’Fuck,’ Rex thought, the word echoing like a death knell in the private chambers of his mind. This isn’t an extension of his power. ’This is her touching the world.’

A distant, almost abstract realization flickered through his pain-addled consciousness. For months, following Lustia’s cautious counsel, he had treated the upper tiers of the divine framework as abstract threat variables to be managed and categories to be studied from a safe remove.

He had treated them like weather patterns. He had not understood, until this exact heartbeat, what it actually felt like to have one of those tiers lean down and press a single finger directly onto the scale of his existence.

The sensation was like standing at the edge of an abyss and feeling, for the first time, not just the drop, but an actual, crushing current pulling at your ankles, threatening to drag you into something endless.
Inside his mind, his Divine Perception screamed as it strained against the incoming tide.

[DURATION: INDETERMINATE]
[MAGNITUDE: EXCEEDS INSTRUMENT CEILING ERROR: DATA NON-QUANTIFIABLE]

Lying in the gore-soaked wreckage of his own body, feeling the wet squelch of his punctured lung with every labored breath, Rex felt something he hadn’t experienced since the dawn of his second life: a small, icy thread of genuine alarm threading through his calculations.
This wasn’t an Apostle drawing on granted authority. This was a direct conduit.

There was no ceiling to locate, no magical clock counting down toward a merciful exhaustion. There was only an open tap, a celestial floodgate held open by a divine will that would keep flowing for exactly as long as she chose to let it.
[INITIATING: FULL POTENTIAL ADAPTATION]
The system roared to life but immediately struck resistance unlike anything in its recorded history.
[ERROR: ADAPTATION PROTOCOL STALLED]
[REASON: LOGIC INSTABILITY DETECTED]
The mechanism refused to resolve. Every previous opponent Rex had ever faced, from Kaeleth’s seventeen shifting temporal variations to Apollo’s own earlier red gold states, had possessed edges.
They had shapes, patterns, and limits that could be mapped, dissected, and eventually covered.
This thing had no edges.

It was a shapeshifter of pure causality. One moment, the pressure expressed itself as raw, overwhelming physical force that threatened to crush Rex’s bones into powder; the next, it shifted into something that pressed directly against his soul register, a metaphysical weight that made his very essence feel like it was being flayed.
Then, it would pivot again, becoming a pure disruption of reality itself, a chaotic energy that operated by no law of physics or magic that Rex could isolate.

The analysis window, which had been compressed to a desperate four seconds during the earlier brutality of their clash, suddenly stretched ten seconds, fifteen seconds, twenty, then snapped back to zero.
The system was caught in an endless loop, attempting to begin its work from nothing each time Apollo’s power mutated into a new form of divinity.
Rex watched through blood-blurred vision as Apollo stood up. The man was gone.
What remained was a silhouette carved out of white gold annihilation, a walking violation of every natural law Rex knew.
’Come on,’ Rex thought, his teeth grinding against the copper taste of his own blood as he braced his failing body. ’Show me your shape.’
’Let me see you...’
’Let me find the edge so I can cut through it.’

’Let me find the edge so I can cut through it.’

chapters.title: Chapter 1181. For the First Time, I Felt the Lag of My Own Immortality
paragraphs: For the first time since he had awakened to this second life, for the first time since he had begun his climb through the ranks of gods and monsters, Rex Rexilion faced a problem he could not measure.
The variables were gone, and the math had failed. There was only the terrifying certainty of approaching annihilation.
Apollo moved.

It wasn’t a run; it was a displacement of reality. One moment he was twenty paces away, a pillar of blinding white gold light; the next, he was a streak of celestial fury that tore through the air with a sound like thunder cracking directly overhead.
BOOM CRACK.
The sheer displacement of air created a vacuum behind him, sucking loose debris and blood mist into his wake.
Rex’s mind screamed at him to move. His battered concentration, fraying like a rope under tension, scraped against the limits of his Foresight.
’Move... Now!’

Through a haze of agony and blood, Rex forced his shattered muscles to obey. He triggered what remained of his [Peak Superhuman Physique], attempting to twist his broken torso and roll away from the inevitable impact.
He could see the fist coming not as a limb, but as a comet of condensed divinity aimed directly at his center.
’Too slow... I’m too fucking slow...’
CRUNCH.
The impact was not just a sound; it was a seismic event. Apollo’s fist connected square with Rex’s abdomen.

The force didn’t just bruise; it reconfigured his biology. Rex felt his abdominal wall collapse inward with a wet, sickening squelch as his intestines, liver, and spleen were compressed into a single, traumatized mass of pulp.
His spine groaned under the sudden hydraulic pressure of the blow.

The force of the strike launched Rex off the ground like a projectile. He became a human bullet, tearing through three separate layers of the domain’s ambient light, each layer shattering like glass SHHHH RING! before he slammed into something solid at the far edge of the space.
A barrier of compressed reality, an invisible wall formed by the collapsing structure itself, caught him with the force of a meteor hitting a mountain.
Rex’s body crumpled against the barrier, his blood painting the invisible surface in a grotesque, spreading fan. His vision swam in crimson, and his lungs felt like they were filled with molten lead.
"You said nothing could kill you," Apollo’s voice descended upon him.
It was no longer human. It was a dual-toned roar, the voice of a man layered atop the terrifying, harmonic resonance of a goddess.
It sounded like two tectonic plates grinding together.
Apollo didn’t wait for Rex to breathe. He didn’t give him the mercy of a second of pain.
He was already moving again, a golden blur closing the distance before Rex’s body had even finished sliding down the barrier.
"Let’s find out how true that claim really is," Apollo hissed.
The assault began. It was a punishing, unrelenting combination that defied the laws of combat.

Apollo’s fist came first with a lightning-fast jab that shattered Rex’s left cheekbone with a wet snap, sending fragments of bone piercing through the skin. Before Rex could even register the pain, a follow-up hook caught him in the ribs. CRACK CRACK CRACK—the sound of multiple ribs splintering like dry kindling.
Each strike was delivered with zero recovery time. Apollo was a machine of divine retribution.

A knee to the sternum that forced the remaining air from Rex’s lungs in a spray of blood; an elbow to the temple that sent stars exploding across Rex’s vision; a palm strike to the chest that felt like being hit by a runaway freight train.
’I can’t... adapt...’ Rex’s inner monologue was drowning in the static of pain. ’Every time I try to map the rhythm, the power shifts.’
’It’s not a combo... it’s a continuous avalanche.’

Blood sprayed from Rex’s mouth with every impact, each blow sending fresh arterial crimson across Apollo’s glowing form. Rex was trapped in a cycle of breaking and bleeding, a human punching bag caught between the earth and a god who had decided that mercy was no longer an option.
What followed stopped resembling a fight in any sense Rex Rexilion would have used the word. "Fight" implied two opposing forces, a contest of skill, a back and forth.
This was not a contest; it was a systematic dismantling. It was a slaughterhouse performance where the butcher had been granted the power of a creator.
Apollo did not pace himself. There was no reason to anymore.

The four-minute guillotine had been removed from his neck. There was no clock ticking toward exhaustion, no mana reserves he needed to husband for a potential escape, and no fear of his own body collapsing under the strain.
That absence of limitation manifested in every single strike. He didn’t swing; he detonated.
He didn’t punch; he erupted. The interval between blows shrank until the space between impacts became microscopic, leaving Rex trapped in a continuous, overlapping cascade of violence.
Rex’s mind raced, desperate, clawing for a solution. ’Telekinesis! Now!’
[ACTIVATE: KINETIC INTERCEPTION]
He threw every remaining ounce of his will into his telekinetic field, trying to create a buffer between himself and the golden comet that was Apollo.

But the system couldn’t keep up. He managed to catch maybe one strike in five, redirecting a fragment of the violet floor to intercept a fist or hastily compressing a barrier of air, but the other four landed clean through his defenses as if they weren’t even there.
CRACK THUD. CRACK THUD.
His body began to come apart in ways it had never come apart before. His biology was being asked to perform miracles just to stay in one piece.
A devastating hook caught Rex across his left flank. The force was so concentrated, so impossibly dense, that it exceeded the tensile strength of his skin and muscle entirely.
A section of his torso simply... tore away. Flesh split like overripe fruit under the pressure of Apollo’s divine weight, exposing raw, pulsing muscle and the wet glint of ribs.
[INFINITE REGENERATION: CRITICAL OVERLOAD]
[RECOVERY TIME: 3.8 SECONDS DELAYED BY CATASTROPHIC CELLULAR TRAUMA]

For the first time in his existence, Rex felt the terrifying lag of his own immortality. His regeneration, which had never once failed to seal a wound in less than a heartbeat, struggled to stitch the gaping wound closed while new trauma kept reopening it.

His right leg buckled with a sound like a tree trunk snapping KRA THOOM as a kick shattered his femur in two places. The bone began to knit back together with agonizing heat, but before the calcium could even fuse, Apollo’s boot came down again, breaking the newly formed bone in three different locations.
’Fuck... I can’t... I can’t find the rhythm...’ Rex’s consciousness flickered like a dying bulb. ’He’s not attacking me anymore.’
’He’s... he’s auditing my destruction.’

Through the haze of crimson pain and the metallic taste of blood filling his throat, Rex recognized something terrifying. The raw, screaming rage that had driven Apollo minutes ago was still there, burning like fuel, but underneath it, something far worse had taken over: a cold, surgical methodology.
Apollo was no longer a man drowning in grief; he had become an instrument of precise annihilation.
Every strike was deliberate. A fist to the sternum that didn’t just bruise but cracked the bone straight through, sending splinters inward toward his heart.
An open palm to the temple that rattled his skull with such frequency that his vision didn’t just blur; it shattered into kaleidoscopic fragments of light and shadow.
Then came the grip.
Apollo’s hand shot forward, seizing Rex by the throat. The fingers didn’t just squeeze; they invaded.

The divine pressure focused entirely on the delicate cartilage of Rex’s windpipe. Rex could hear the wet, grinding sound of his own larynx collapsing under fingers that no longer felt like they belonged to a healer.
They felt like heated iron pistons.
"Does it hurt, Rex?" Apollo asked, his voice a terrifying harmony of two souls screaming in unison.
His face was inches away, beautiful and horrific, glowing with a light that promised nothing but the end. "Does it feel like the story is finally ending?"
Rex tried to speak, tried to spit blood in defiance, but all that came out was a wet, gurgling wheeze as his throat gave way under the divine weight.

chapters.title: Chapter 1182. Strangers Can’t Hurt Each Other This Thoroughly
paragraphs: Rex tried three separate times to create distance—three desperate attempts to reclaim even an inch of space—and each failure felt like another nail being driven into his coffin.
The first attempt was a telekinetic pulse, a concentrated wave of force designed to shatter bone and throw a mountain backward. Rex channeled everything into it, expecting a satisfying recoil.

Instead, the wave washed over Apollo like water over polished marble. The divine channel had rendered Apollo functionally immune to displacement; he was no longer a body subject to physics but an anchor point for reality itself. He didn’t even stagger.
The second attempt was more desperate: a burst of that unclassifiable, chaotic elemental frequency, the same raw distortion that had once dissolved three stacked barrier workings in a single pass.
Rex unleashed it in a searing arc, expecting to see Apollo’s skin blister or his divine aura fracture. The energy washed over Apollo’s luminous skin with a pathetic hiss, producing nothing.
No burn, no flinch, not even the courtesy of a delayed reaction. It was like throwing pebbles at a hurricane.
The third was a last resort: a localized gravity spike, meant to pin Apollo to the floor with enough force to crater the entire domain. For half a second, it worked.
The ground beneath Apollo cracked as the pressure intensified. Then, with a sound like tearing silk, Ssssshhhhhk, the open divine channel simply overrode the spell.
Apollo didn’t struggle against the gravity; he simply walked through the compressed space as though it were ordinary air, each step grinding the stone beneath him into fine dust.
Apollo closed the distance in three strides, his fist connecting with Rex’s jaw in a wet, bone-splintering crack. CRUNCH.
"Do you feel pain now?" Apollo asked between blows.

His eyes had changed; the warm gold had been consumed, leaving behind two burning pits of saturated, blood-red fury. He watched the wreckage of Rex’s body—the torn flesh, the exposed bone, and the spreading crimson pool—with a hollow satisfaction that lacked any trace of the man who had once offered comfort at a funeral.
"Are you afraid now, Rex? Or whatever your real name actually is?"
Apollo’s fist came again, a gut punch that made Rex’s vision go white.

Even now, even with his left arm bent at an angle that defied every law of anatomy, the bone protruding through the skin in a jagged white spike, Rex forced a laugh. It was a wet, gurgling sound that sprayed blood across his own lips.
His eyes stayed open, fixed on Apollo’s face with a terrifying, unshakable certainty.
"My name... is Rex," he wheezed, the words barely audible through the blood filling his throat. "That’s never changed."
"I never hid it from you, Apollo."
"You simply... never looked closely enough to see it."
Apollo’s next strike was a backhand that sent Rex spinning.
"Stop saying my name like that!" Apollo roared, his voice shaking with something far more dangerous than rage; it was a raw, bleeding vulnerability. "Like we’re still friends!"
"Like any of this is still a conversation between two people who know each other!"
Rex dragged himself upright, his movements mechanical, pained, but stubbornly defiant. His grin didn’t falter, even as blood ran freely down his chin, dripping onto his ruined chest.
"We are two people who know each other." Rex’s voice steadied for a heartbeat, carrying a chilling calm despite the carnage of his body. "That’s rather the entire point, Apollo."
"I know you better than anyone alive... I know what makes you angry, I know what makes you kind... and I know exactly which of your own weaknesses will hurt you the most if I press on them."
Rex leaned forward slightly, despite the agony, his eyes locking onto Apollo’s crimson gaze.
"Strangers can’t hurt each other this thoroughly, Apollo."
"You can’t break a man’s spirit with just fists and magic... It takes genuine intimacy to do what I’ve done to you today."
"I didn’t just fight you... I tore through everything you believed you were...!"
Apollo did not answer with words. He answered with violence.
A knee driven upward with the force of a collapsing star connected squarely with Rex’s sternum.
CRUNCH SHHHH.

The sound was wet and hollow as three more ribs snapped simultaneously, the jagged bone fragments grinding against each other like broken glass. The impact drove every last molecule of oxygen from Rex’s lungs in a spray of crimson mist.
Before the air could even attempt to return, Apollo followed through with a vicious, downward elbow to Rex’s jaw.
WHACK.
The force was so obscene that Rex’s head twisted nearly one hundred and eighty degrees on his neck, his vision exploding into a static-filled void.
For a heartbeat, Rex hung limp, his consciousness flickering like a candle in a hurricane, suspended only by Apollo’s white knuckled grip on his ruined collar.
’Come on... adapt... find the gap... find one fucking gap...’ Rex’s mind screamed through the static.
[SYSTEM CRITICAL: KINETIC OVERLOAD]
[ADAPTATION PROTOCOL: PARTIAL SUCCESS KINETIC REDIRECTION ENGAGED]

As Apollo wound up for a killing blow, a fist glowing with enough divine heat to melt steel, aimed directly at the ribcage that had already been shattered twice, Rex found his opening. It was a microscopic window, a desperate gamble born of pure instinct.
At the last possible millisecond, Rex poured every remaining scrap of his telekinetic will into a single, focused point. He didn’t try to stop the blow; he simply nudged it.
’Just three inches... just three inches to the left...’

The divine fist tore through the air with a scream like rending metal. Because of Rex’s last-second intervention, the impact missed his punctured lung by a fraction of an inch, slamming instead into the already pulverized muscle of his flank.

The pain was so intense it transcended feeling; it became a pure, white noise that drowned out reality. It bought him four seconds of precious, agonizing survival, but the reprieve was meaningless; the next strike arrived with such devastating momentum that the correction was rendered irrelevant anyway.

Apollo hauled Rex upright by the collar with one hand, lifting his broken body off the fractured ground. The divine energy flowing through Apollo’s veins burned with such terrifying intensity that it cast a long, harsh, jagged shadow across the domain’s floor, a shadow that looked more like a demon than a man.

The face staring at Rex was no longer that of the healer, the protector, or the friend. Every trace of restraint, every shred of the compassion that Aethelgard had built its faith around, had been incinerated.
In its place was something primal and ancient: a mountain of hatred born from the deepest, most corrosive betrayal a soul could endure.
"I am going to end you here," Apollo said.
His voice was low, vibrating with a terrifying, quiet certainty that was far more frightening than his earlier roars. "Now... Today... And I will not regret a single moment of it..."

Rex dangled there, his body a marionette of broken bones and torn sinew. His ribcage was visibly wrong beneath the tattered remains of his skin, shifting grotesquely with every shallow, bubbling breath.
He tried to nod, but his neck refused to cooperate, his vertebrae grinding against each other in protest.
Instead, he simply stared into those crimson depths. A bloody, defiant grin split his face.
"Good," Rex rasped, the word coming out as a wet gurgle through the blood coating his teeth. "I was starting to worry... you’d talk yourself out of it... before we got to the interesting part."

Then, with a roar that sounded like the death of a star, Apollo drove that point of condensed annihilation straight into the center of Rex’s chest.
BOOOOOOOM!!!
The impact did not simply hurt him. It did not merely break him, but it went through him.

The blast tore outward from the point of contact in a devastating spherical wave of pure force. The shockwave flattened everything within thirty meters, shredding through the remaining intact sections of the domain floor like tissue paper.

Fault lines screamed across the landscape, racing toward the edges of a space that had never truly possessed proper boundaries. Somewhere in the distance, unseen by either combatant, an entire quadrant of the domain simply... ceased to exist.
It winked out of reality, the structural integrity finally collapsing under a pressure it had never been built to withstand.
Rex’s body acted as the lightning rod for this cosmic fury. He absorbed the full, unmitigated force directly into his sternum.
For one genuinely uncertain moment, something inside Rex that had never once stopped working the fundamental rhythm of his existence simply stopped.
His heart did not beat.
The world went silent. The screams of the breaking floor, the roaring of Apollo’s power, and the blood rushing in his ears—all of it vanished into a terrifying, absolute vacuum.

His heart sat there, motionless, silent, for nearly three full seconds. In that void, [INFINITE REGENERATION] fought a war against damage on a scale it had never been asked to repair in a single instant.
It was a desperate, microscopic struggle to stitch together atoms that had been scattered by divine force.
Those three seconds were, without exaggeration, the closest thing to actual death Rex had experienced since the fall from that balcony that had ended his first life.
There was no thought in them. There was no pain, no anger, no fear, just a black, hollow interval where Rex Rexilion ceased to be.
Then, the interval ended.
THUMP THUMP.

His heart restarted with such violent, uncontrolled force that it arched his entire ruined body off the crater floor. It was not a gentle revival; it was a resurrection that felt like being struck by lightning from the inside out.

The sudden rush of blood through shattered vessels and torn arteries was a new kind of agony, a searing, electrical torment that made the previous beating feel like a mercy. Rex’s back convulsed, his spine cracking as his body fought to reassert its own existence against the void.
Rex’s eyes snapped open again. When they did, they opened into a body that was, by any reasonable measure of biology, complete wreckage.

His chest cavity looked like something that had been put through an industrial shredder; the skin was charred in places, torn open in others, revealing the wet, grinding machinery of his ribs attempting to fuse back together.

Apollo stood over him, his chest heaving in ragged, desperate gasps. The last of the open divine channel was guttering out of him now, flickering like a candle drowning in its own wax after that catastrophic expenditure of power.

He stared down at Rex’s sternum, the place that had just, for three excruciating seconds, been a motionless tomb. His eyes widened as he watched the flesh twitch, saw the blood pulse once more through the shattered vessels, and witnessed the impossible: the chest began to rise and fall again.
"How..." Apollo whispered, the word cracking.
His hands were shaking, the divine glow fading to reveal fingers stained with Rex’s blood. "How are you still alive? That should have been enough to kill a god..."
"That should have erased your very soul from existence."
Rex pushed himself up onto one elbow. The movement was agonizingly slow.

Each motion produced a wet, grinding sound, SKRITCH CRUNCH, as his vertebrae realigned themselves mid-movement. His body was knitting itself back together in desperate, uneven fits and starts, the regeneration struggling to prioritize wounds that were simply too extensive to be solved in a single heartbeat.
When he finally spoke, his voice was a wrecked, gravelly rasp, but the calm beneath it remained infuriatingly, maliciously the same calm it had been from the moment they first drew blood.
"I told you already," Rex said, blood frothing at the corner of his mouth. "You can’t kill me that way, Apollo...
"No matter how much power you bring to bear... No matter how many stars you throw at me..."
"WHY?" Apollo screamed.

The sound wasn’t human; it was a primal howl of frustration that tore through the remaining air. The sheer volume of his agony cracked something in the fabric of the domain itself. KRA KOOM and fresh spiderweb fractures raced outward from where he stood, spidering across the reality they occupied.
"Why can nothing kill you?! Are you some kind of monster? Are you actually immortal?!"
Rex looked up at him. In that moment, something in his expression shifted. The mocking edge, the playful cruelty, fell away, replaced by a colder, more calculating stillness.
It was the look of a man weighing whether to hand over a truth and deciding that the revelation would be more devastating than any physical blow Apollo had left in him.
There was a perverse pleasure in the calculation, a recognition that this truth would do more damage to Apollo’s sanity than any fist could ever manage.
"No," Rex said softly, his eyes locking onto Apollo’s crimson gaze. "I’m not immortal in the way your simplistic mind is imagining."
"But to actually kill me, Apollo... you can’t simply destroy this body."
"This flesh is just... scaffolding."
He paused, letting the implication hang in the air like poisonous smoke, savoring the way Apollo’s expression began to fracture into confusion and horror.
"You would have to kill every woman who has ever become mine," Rex continued, his voice growing steadier, more resonant despite the blood thick in his throat. "Every maximum bond I hold is a tether."
"Every soul I have claimed is a pillar that supports this existence."
"They are the fuel for my regeneration... They are the reason I cannot die..."
Rex took a breath, each one a wet rattle, and began to recite them like a litany of sins.
"Talyra... Aisella... Nerith... Mireya... Mara... Marceline... Lily... Diana... Elizabeth... Elaris... Aurelia... Iris... Morwenna... Cassandra... Gorvasha... Viscaria... Lilith... and more..."

chapters.title: Chapter 1184. He Had Been Inflicted With Nothing More Than a List of Names
paragraphs: Rex let the silence stretch, thick and poisonous, watching with predator-like focus as each name landed like a fresh blade twisting in Apollo’s chest.
He could see the gears turning behind Apollo’s bloodshot eyes, the horrifying realization dawning as the list moved from strangers to allies to something far more intimate.
"And your mother," Rex finished, his voice dropping to a conspiratorial murmur that somehow carried further than his earlier screams. "Amelia."
The name hung between them like a guillotine blade.

The color drained from Apollo’s face in slow, nauseating degrees, leaving him a ghastly, waxen pale beneath the dried blood spatter. His mouth opened, his throat working convulsively, but no sound came out, only a pathetic, wet wheeze.
The divine energy still clinging to his skin didn’t flare with power; instead, it shuddered and flickered like a dying lamp, responding to the full body tremor that now wracked his frame.

Every ounce of certainty that had carried Apollo through the slaughter, every conviction that had fueled his righteous fury, collapsed instantly into a hollow, directionless despair. The path to the vengeance he craved—the singular purpose that had kept him upright while his world burned—had just been revealed as a trap.

To kill Rex, he would not simply be a liberator or a judge; he would be a butcher. He would have to become the very monster he sought to destroy, systematically executing every woman he had ever protected, every friend he had ever held dear, ending with the mother who had taught him what kindness was.
’No... no, that’s impossible... he’s lying... he has to be lying...’ Apollo’s mind shrieked, but there was no comfort to be found in his own thoughts.
His intellect, sharp and divine, betrayed him by confirming the truth. Rex wasn’t bluffing.
The metaphysical tether was real. The cost was absolute.

Apollo tried, once, to find an argument against it. His lips moved silently for several seconds, his brain frantically scanning for a flaw in the logic, a loophole, a hidden weakness in Rex’s claim that would allow him to keep the version of vengeance he had been building since the day his world shattered.
He searched for a way to kill Rex without becoming a demon.
But there was nothing. The silence of the domain seemed to mock him, echoing the emptiness in his own soul.

He understood then, with the devastating clarity that comes only at the absolute bottom of a person’s capacity to endure, that Rex had not offered this information out of some twisted sense of honesty.
Rex hadn’t been sharing a secret; he had been deploying a weapon. Every name had been chosen with surgical precision; every pause between them had been measured to maximize the psychological trauma.

Rex wasn’t trying to win a fight anymore; he was winning a war of attrition against Apollo’s very humanity. He wanted Apollo to stand there, broken and bleeding, knowing that his only path to justice was a corridor lined with the corpses of everyone he loved.
Rex began to rise.
It started as a grotesque display of biological reconstruction.
CRACK POP. SHHHH TICK.
One broken joint reset itself with a wet snap, followed by the grinding and sliding sounds of vertebrae reassembling.

At first, it was agonizingly slow, but then something shifted. The healing accelerated with terrifying purpose, the pace of his regeneration surging past its earlier limits as though the very effort required to maintain the illusion of being wounded had become beneath him.

Whatever restraint Rex had been exercising throughout this entire butchery, the deliberate, calculated choice to absorb bone-breaking impacts and organ-crushing blows just to harvest data on Apollo’s divine mechanism ended in that instant.
He had learned what he needed to know about the architecture of the open channel, and continuing to play the victim was no longer a strategy; it was an indulgence he could no longer afford.
’Data acquisition complete,’ Rex’s mind hummed, cold and detached behind his eyes. ’The divine conduit is a finite resource.’
’A massive one, yes, but finite nonetheless.’
He could see the truth written in Apollo’s failing body. The divine channel Apollo had tapped into was not an infinite well, despite its terrifying display.

That final, apocalyptic strike that had stopped Rex’s own heart had been a catastrophic withdrawal from a cosmic bank account, a debt Apollo’s own flesh was now paying in real time. The pallor spreading across Apollo’s face wasn’t just shock; it was exhaustion.

The visible tremor in his stance wasn’t fear; it was the collapse of his spiritual stamina. Whatever goddess had opened that door had not done so without a price, and she had deliberately withheld the location of the limit from her vessel.
’Elegant cruelty,’ Rex thought with a flicker of genuine appreciation. ’Very well played, Goddess.’
Then came the flood.
VROOOOOOM.

Peak Superhuman Physique flooded back through muscle fibers that had been shredded into ribbons minutes earlier. The regeneration didn’t just restore him to function; it drove him to full, lethal output.
His muscles coiled with new, dense power, his tendons tightening like steel cables. Simultaneously, the violet-black aura of his Lustful Villain identity erupted from his pores.

It didn’t just flicker; it climbed around him in a steadily building corona of shadow and malice, burning brighter and more oppressive than at any other point in the engagement. The darkness seemed to drink the little light that remained in the domain.

When Rex finally stood fully upright, there was no trace of the wreckage Apollo had spent the last hour producing. There was no blood dripping from his chin, no labored breathing, and no twisted ribcage.
He stood as a monument of perfect, predatory vitality.
The shift in pressure was immediate. The air around them grew heavy, charged with a static that made the hair on Apollo’s arms stand up.
"You know, Apollo," Rex said.

His voice was no longer a gravelly rasp or a death rattle. It had returned entirely to its usual level of calm, a smooth, terrifyingly composed baritone that cut through the silence of the ruined domain like a scalpel. "I have let you feel like you had a chance for long enough now.
Rex took a single step forward, the violet-black aura pulsing with every heartbeat.
"I think you’ve suffered enough to earn your final lesson."
Apollo did not answer. He could not.

The words Rex had spoken—the names, the implications, the horrific price of victory—were lodged in his throat like shards of broken glass. He stood frozen in the center of the shattered domain, a fallen monument to a divine purpose that had been systematically dismantled.

The last of the divine channel had not merely drained; it had been violently evacuated from his system, leaving his veins feeling like hollow, frozen conduits. There was no reserve left anywhere in his body.

No spark of holy fire, no residual warmth, no hidden wellspring of courage. He was a husk, a spent shell of a man, his face still drained of color from the psychic mutilation. Rex had been inflicted with nothing more than a list of names.
For one heartbeat, Apollo believed he might still be able to summon something or anything to deflect what was coming.
He tried to call upon the light, to scrape the bottom of his soul for one last defensive barrier, but there was only a cold, yawning emptiness where his power used to live.
The fight that had briefly, impossibly, turned in his favor had not just shifted; it had collapsed, imploded, the instant Rex decided that the game was over.
Rex moved.
There was no wind-up.
No warning shout.
No dramatic gathering of energy.
There was only the sudden, terrifying displacement of air as Rex launched himself forward.
WHOOSH!!

He came forward at a speed that Apollo’s exhausted, traumatized senses could barely track. To Apollo’s failing vision, Rex didn’t seem to run; he seemed to simply exist in one space and then suddenly exist in another, closer to him.
The violet black corona of Rex’s aura tore through the air like a physical blade, leaving behind a trail of distorted reality that screamed with malevolent energy.

Apollo’s pupils dilated, his heart hammering a weak, panicked rhythm against his ribs. Time seemed to dilate, stretching the seconds into agonizing minutes as he watched the predator close the distance.

He could see the minute details now: the terrifyingly calm expression on Rex’s face, the way the shadows coiled around his fist like living serpents, and the absolute certainty in every muscle twitch.
’Move,’ Apollo’s mind screamed. ’Gods, please, just let me move...’
But his limbs were leaden, and his reflexes shattered. The last thing he saw before the world exploded into violence was not a god, but the inevitable conclusion of his own failure.

chapters.title: Chapter 1185. Everything You’ve Conquered Has Surprised You at Least Once
paragraphs: Rex did not merely attack; he orchestrated a symphony of anatomical destruction. His Martial Arts Mastery and Weapons Mastery had fused with his Telekinesis Full Potential in a terrifying display of synchronized violence.

Every physical movement was augmented by an invisible, crushing layer of telekinetic force, meaning every strike didn’t just land; it arrived from two directions at once: the fist itself and the gravitational pressure surrounding it.
CRUNCH.
A single punch to Apollo’s ribs didn’t require a wind-up or an exchange of blows. There was no struggle, no desperate parry.

There was only the immediate, wet sound of structural failure as the ribs caved inward like dried kindling, piercing the lung tissue. Apollo gasped, a spray of crimson mist erupting from his lips, but Rex was already moving.
A follow-up kick swept through the air, reinforced by telekinetic momentum, and caught Apollo’s raised arm.
SNAP CRACK.
The ulna shattered cleanly, the bone splintering under the sheer force, leaving Apollo’s limb hanging at an impossible, nauseating angle.
Desperation finally overcame Apollo’s shock. With a guttural roar of pure, exhausted instinct, he threw one final counter—a wild, telegraphed swing fueled by the last embers of his divine heritage.
Rex didn’t dodge.
He didn’t retreat. He simply reached out and caught Apollo’s fist in his palm.
The contact was absolute. Apollo pulled, his muscles straining until they quivered, but Rex held the fist as if it were anchored to the bedrock of the universe.
Apollo could feel it then—the absolute, soul-crushing futility of his resistance. He was a child trying to move a mountain.
Then, the torment began.
CRACK.
Rex’s grip tightened. The first finger snapped. Rex didn’t flinch; he didn’t rush.
He held the broken digit still, letting the sound reverberate through the silent domain, letting Apollo feel the white-hot lightning of nerve pain before moving to the next.
CRACK. CRACK. CRACK.

Rex maintained unwavering eye contact the entire time, his dark gaze fixed on Apollo’s watering eyes, forcing him to witness his own degradation. Each break came with its own measured pause, a deliberate cruelty designed to let the agony marinate.

Apollo’s breathing became a series of ragged, wet hitches. He wanted to scream, but his voice seemed to have abandoned him, leaving only the pathetic sounds of a man whose spirit was being systematically dismantled alongside his bones.
"You spent your whole life trying to be a hero," Rex said, his voice conversational even as he drove a fist into Apollo’s jaw.
The blow was reinforced with Gravity Manipulation, multiplying its mass tenfold.
WHAM!
Apollo’s head snapped sideways with enough force to liquify brain tissue. Blood sprayed across the cracked ground as his jaw dislocated with a sickening THUD.

"Trying to protect everyone... Trying to be the shield, the light, the righteous sword," Rex continued, weaving another strike into the rhythm of the beating. "And look at you now... Broken... Pathetic..."
"You can’t even protect yourself, let alone anyone you love...
"Your ideals didn’t save them, Apollo... And they won’t save you."
Apollo collapsed to his knees, his body folding under its own weight. Blood poured freely from his mouth, painting his chin crimson.
The fire that had burned behind his eyes during his brief rampage had been extinguished by that divine fury. In its place was something far more terrifying: a hollow, quiet resignation.
He was a man who had run out of everything except the simple, agonizing fact of still being conscious.
Rex crouched in front of him, bringing his face level with Apollo’s. The violet-black aura pulsed between them like a heartbeat.
"You’ve lost, Apollo," Rex whispered, the words cold as a tombstone. "No goddess is coming to save you now."
"No divine channel remains to bail you out... No options... No miracles..."
"You have exactly one road left from here, and it’s accepting that everything you believed in was a lie."
For a long moment, there was only the sound of Apollo’s wet, labored breathing. Then, slowly and agonizingly, Apollo raised his head.
It cost him visibly. Each inch of movement seemed to fight against gravity itself.
His breath came in ragged, bubbling gasps, but as his eyes met Rex’s, something flickered in the depths of those bloodshot irises. It wasn’t hope; it was something harder.
Something older.
The ghost of the man who had stood before four thousand soldiers and promised them salvation.
His gaze did not flinch.
"Maybe," Apollo said. His voice was weak, shredded by pain and blood, but the tremor was gone. "Maybe I have lost today..."
"Maybe you really are going to kill me here, in this godforsaken place where no one will ever know the truth of what happened."
He paused, drawing a breath that clearly tore through his damaged lungs.
"But you’re wrong if you think this ends with me," he continued, his voice gaining a razor-sharp edge of defiance. "I’m not the first Apostle of Life, Rex..."
"And I promise you... I won’t be the last."
Rex’s eyebrow rose slightly. Behind the reforming edges of the mask, a shadowy lattice of violet energy was weaving itself back across his features like living smoke; his curiosity was genuine.
He didn’t cut Apollo off. He didn’t strike.
He simply watched, fascinated by the way a dying animal could still find the breath to snarl.
"The Goddess of Life won’t let what you’ve done here simply pass," Apollo said.
His voice was gaining a strange, eerie strength, a hard-won timbre that seemed to vibrate from his very bones rather than his throat.

His body was a wreck; blood leaked from his split lips, his ribs grated against one another with every shallow inhale, and his shattered arm twitched uselessly, but his conviction had become his only remaining fuel.
"She has seen all of this... Every drop of blood, every broken bone, every violation of the natural order."
Apollo coughed, sending a spray of crimson across the cracked floor between them. "She knows what you did to me."
"She knows what you threatened to do to my mother, to everyone I loved."
"And someday..." His gaze sharpened, piercing through the violet haze of Rex’s aura. "Someday she will choose a new Apostle..."
"Someone stronger than I was... Someone more prepared... Someone who will come for you in a way you cannot lie your way around..."
"Someone who cannot be manipulated or talked down with a clever enough story... A force that doesn’t negotiate."
Rex tilted his head, studying the broken man with something that looked almost like respect layered beneath a veneer of cold mockery.
"You say that as though it frightens me," he said, his voice smooth as silk over gravel. "It doesn’t..."
"I’ve already fought one god and taken a piece of him home with me as a souvenir..."
"If your goddess sends me another, I’ll simply add whatever they give me to the collection."

"You say that now." Apollo’s voice cracked on the last word, but the shape of the sentence remained defiant. "You said the same thing about the Apostle network before you found out how deep the rot actually went..."
"You said it about the Underlayer before you discovered how much of it you’d have to burn to the ground just to stand on the ashes."
A ghost of a smile touched Apollo’s bloodied mouth. "Everything you’ve conquered so far has surprised you at least once before you finished conquering it..."
"You play the game like you know all the rules, Rex, but you’re still playing..."
"Maybe this will be the same..."
"Maybe you’ll finally meet something that doesn’t bend the way you expect... Something that breaks you instead."
Rex laughed. It was softer this time, lighter than the cruel amusement from earlier, almost genuine, but underneath that amusement, a small, razor-thin thread of wariness coiled in his gut.
He didn’t let it show on his face. He was too seasoned for that.

"I’ll look forward to it," Rex said, his voice carrying the casual finality of a death sentence. "Truly... But until that day comes, Apollo, you’re going to be nothing more than the memory of a hero who failed to protect anything that mattered to him..."
"A cautionary tale."
The light in Apollo’s eyes began to dim, the last reserves of his spiritual and physical stamina finally hemorrhaging away. His head drooped slightly, but his gaze never wavered from Rex’s mask.
"Maybe," Apollo whispered, his voice fading into a wet rasp. "But at least I’ll die knowing I never stopped believing that goodness exists."
"Even if..." A final, shuddering breath escaped him. "...even if it wasn’t enough to beat you today."
